description:
Given an array of words, print all anagrams together.
 For example, if the given array is {“cat”, “dog”, “tac”, “god”, “act”}, then output may be “cat tac act dog god”.
inputFormat: First line consists of T test case. First line of every test case consists of N, denoting the number of words in array. Second line of every test case consists of words of array.
outputFormat: Single line output, print the counts of anagrams in increasing order.
sampleInput:
2
5
act cat tac god dog
3
act cat tac

name: Print Permutations
description: Given a string, print all permutations of a given string.
inputFormat: Take Input the String.
outputFormat: For each test case, print all permutations of a given string S with single space
sampleOutput: ABSG ABGS ASBG ASGB AGSB AGBS BASG BAGS BSAG BSGA BGSA BGAS SBAG SBGA SABG SAGB SGAB SGBA GBSA GBAS GSBA GSAB GASB GABS

name: Smallest window with characters
description:
Given a string 's'. The task is to find the smallest window length that contains all the characters of the given string at least one time.
For eg. A = “aabcbcdbca”, then the result would be 4 as of the smallest window will be “dbca”.
inputFormat:
The first line of input contains an integer T denoting the no of test cases.

Then T test cases follow. Each test case contains a string S.
outputFormat: For each test case in a new line print the length of the smallest such string.

name: Smallest window in a string
description: Given a string S and text t. Output the smallest window in the string having all characters of the text. Both the string and text contains small case letters.
inputFormat:
First line contains T , the number of test cases.

Each test contains 2 lines having a string S and t.
outputFormat:
Output the smallest window of the string containing all the characters of the text.

If such window doesn`t exist or this task can not be done then print -1.

name: largest palindrome
description: Given a string containing all digits, we need to convert this string to a palindrome by changing at most K digits. If many solutions are possible then print lexicographically largest one.
inputFormat:
The First Line contains an Integer T, as number of Testcases.
Next Line contains a String str and an Integer which is k.
outputFormat:
Print the palindromic String for each test case separated by a newLine.

If Palindromic String cannot be form then print - "Not possible".

name: Vertex Tour
description: Given an adjacency matrix representation of a graph, you need to find if there exists a path that visits each vertex of the graph exactly once.
inputFormat: A 2D array graph[V][V] where V is the number of vertices in graph and graph[V][V] is adjacency matrix representation of the graph. A value graph[i][j] is 1 if there is a direct edge from i to j, otherwise graph[i][j] is 0
outputFormat: Print "Yes" if there exist such path otherwise print "No" (Without quotes)

name: Aquaman And The Trident
description: Aquaman after his defeat from the ocean master is out in search of the Trident of Atlan. In his quest to the trident, Mera gave him the key to defeating The Trench army (an army of mutated Atlanteans who became monstrous cannibals long ago). She told Aquaman then the Leader of The Trench army will give him two numbers A and B. To save himself from the deadly attack of the Trench army and get the Trident he is supposed to find all the unique possible combination of natural numbers sum of whose Bth power is equal to A. Aquaman is supposed to print all the unique combinations in sorted order with each combination in a new line and also print the total number of such combinations in the last line. Help Aquaman in his quest to the Trident.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer A.
The second line contains an integer B.
outputFormat: Print all the unique combinations in sorted order and separated by space with each combination in a new line and also print the total number of such combinations in the last line.

name: Tri Wizard Cup
description:
Harry Potter is now in the last stage of his quest to the tri-wizard cup which will make him the winner of the tri-wizard tournament. In the last stage all the finalist along with Harry Potter are supposed to cross a maze(Matrix) of MxN size. Every participant will start from the top left corner (i.e {0,0} index) and are given a destinative coordinate {x, y} where the cup is present. Every candidate can move to the adjacent coordinate from where they are standing and can't move diagonally. Only left, right, up and down movements are allowed. But along with the Triwizard cup, Voldemort and his army are ready to attack Harry at some coordinates. Now you have to help harry to reach the final destination without going to the coordinate where Voldemort's army is standing. You have to find the length of the longest possible path that Harry can travel in order to win the competition. If the Voldemort's army is present at the final destination you can find a possible path(isn't that obvious)
(Consider 0 based indexing)
constraints:
The product of M and N will be less than 30.
X and Y will always lie in the range of M and N
inputFormat:
The first line of the input will contain two integers M and N denoting the size of the matrix maze.
following next M lines will contain N integers each which will be either 0 or 1 where 0 denotes the presence of Voldemort's Army.
Next line will contain two integers X and Y denoting the final destination where the cup is present.
outputFormat: The length of the longest possible path to reach the destination from the top left. Print -1 if no such path exists.

name: Garima Mam and the Challenge
description:
Ms Garima is an Instructor at Coding Blocks. She is a very hardworking Teacher and tries her best to teach the students. Now, Ms Garima and her Teaching Assistant are shortlisting the questions-topicwise for the next batch of java at coding blocks. They have already shortlisted questions for nearly all topics except a topic with tag Strings and Recursion, Ms Garima suggest to include the question of palindrome but suddenly the assistant told her it is a too easy question to include. So She develops the palindromic Question with some Twist. Inorder to publish the question she want her assistant to write code for the solution of the Question. She gave him a challenge of palindromic SubStrings Using Recursion. The challenge is, Given a String the Job is to return an ArrayList of ArrayList containing all possible palindromic Substrings Using Recursion but here comes the twist and which is you need to print the Palindromic substrings in a different way refer sample input Output Case to Understand the twist of the Question.
Now on behalf of the assistant, Write a recursive function that can solve the Given Challenge.
inputFormat:
The First Line Contains the Number of Test Cases.
Next Line contains a String.
outputFormat: Print the ArrayList of ArrayList of the palindromic Substrings.
sampleOutput:
[[n, i, t, i, n], [n, iti, n], [nitin]]
[[a, b, a, c, a], [a, b, aca], [aba, c, a]]

name: Find Missing Number In A Sorted Array
description: Given a list of n-1 integers and these integers are in the range of 1 to n. There are no duplicates in list. One of the integers is missing in the list. Write an efficient code to find the missing integer.
inputFormat:
First Line contains N-1, which is the number of integers in range from 1 to N.
Next Line contains N-1 integers in sorted order.
outputFormat: Print the missing number from array in range 1 to N.

name: Garima Mam and the Kid
description:
Ms Garima is a Talented Mentor at coding blocks and even works on Holidays in order to Teach students every aspect of the Course. On the new year's eve, she has placed a Doubt class and the batch is going to start in 15 mins. Suddenly Priyanka Mam, one of our Coding Blocks Family Member came with her daughter Arpita, She is a very sweet 7 year old kid and loves to Solve Puzzles. Now Priyanka mam has to go outside for some work but cannot take Arpita with her. So she seeks help from Garima mam. As she is very Kind, she is ready to help her and after talking to her Priyanka mam left for work. But Garima mam also has to take her class so She gave Arpita a puzzle in order to get her busy with the puzzle. She has given Arpita an Array of N numbers. Now Arpita needs to find that the length of longest subarray with first element greater than or equal to the Last element.

Garima mam cannot play with her or check if she has found the right one because of the doubt class. So she writes a program which tells the corresponding answer for each Array.
On behalf of Garima mam you job is to write the given program.
inputFormat:
The First Line contains an Integer which is number of Test-cases.
 Next Line contains an Integer N.
Next Line contains N Integers separated by space.
outputFormat: Print the length of the longest subarray for each test case separated by a new Line.

name: Kth Smallest sum
description: Given an sorted array of positive numbers our tasks is to find the kth smallest sum of continuous subarray.
inputFormat:
The First Line contains an Integer T, as the number of Test cases.
Next Line contains two Integers N and K, as the size of the Array and the value of k.
Next Line contains N Integers separated by Spaces.
outputFormat: Print the Sum of the Kth Smallest Sum for each test case separated by new Line.

name: Longest Subarray with Sum
description: Given an array of N integers. The task is to find the maximum length subarray such that the sum of all its elements is greater than or equal to 0.
inputFormat:
The First Line contains an Integer as the number of Test cases.

The next line contains an Integer N, as the Size of the array.

Next Line contains N Integers separated by space.
outputFormat: Print the max length of the  subarray for each Test Case separated by a new Line.

name: Median of Two Arrays
description:
Given Two sorted arrays A and B of size m and n respectively. Find the median of the two sorted arrays.

__Note:__Try to do the problem in runtime complexity O(log (m+n)).
constraints: Both the Arrays for each of the Test case should be Sorted.
inputFormat:
The First Line contains an Integer T, as the number of test cases.
Next Line contains two Integers m and n. as the size of the arrays.
Next Two Lines contains m and n Integers respectively separated by space.
outputFormat: Print the median for both the arrays separated by new Line.

name: Remove duplicates from an unsorted linked list
description: Given an unsorted linked list remove duplicate nodes from this list and then print the remaining list.
inputFormat:
First line contains N, the number of nodes in the linked list.

Next line contains the N nodes of linked list.
outputFormat: Print the linked list after removing duplicates from the unsorted linked list.

name: Delete Nodes - LL
description: Given a singly linked list delete all nodes which are having a greater value among any of the nodes residing on the right side.
inputFormat:
First line contains N, the number of  nodes in the linked list.

Next line contains the N nodes data .
outputFormat: Print the linked list after deleting the nodes which are having a greater value on right side.

name: Sort a Linked List of 0's,1's and 2's.
description: Given a linked list containing only 0's, 1's and 2's, sort it.
inputFormat:
First line contains N, number of nodes in linked list.
Next line contains N nodes with 0, 1 and 2 data values.
outputFormat: Print the sorted list.

name: Sort Linked List (Absolute Values are sorted)
description: Sort a given linked list which is already sorted on it's absolute values.
inputFormat:
First line contains N, number of nodes in linked list.
Next line contains N nodes sorted on absolute values .
outputFormat: Print the sorted list.

name: Implement two Stacks in an array
description: Given an array say arr, implement two stacks in arr. Perform the desired push, pop and display operations on both the stacks.
inputFormat:
First line contains the size of the array arr,N.

Next line contains n1 and n2, the number of elements in stack1 and stack2 respectively.

Next line contains elements in stack1.

Next line conains elements in stack2.
outputFormat:
Print popped element from stack1 and stack2. Then in the next two lines print the elements of stack1 and stack2 respectively.

If stack is empty then print None.
sampleOutput:
2
5
Elements in stack1 are
1 
Elements in stack2 are
4 3

name: Sum of two Linked Lists
description: Given two numbers represented by two linked lists, write a program that prints the sum list. The sum list is linked list representation of addition of two input numbers in linked lists. It is not allowed to modify the lists. Also, not allowed to use explicit extra space (Use Recursion).
inputFormat:
First line contains **N**,**M**, number of nodes in the 1st and 2nd list.

Next line contains N nodes of 1st list.

Next line contains M nodes of 2nd list.
outputFormat: Print the sum list after adding the two linked lists.

name: Implement stack using a priority queue
description: Implement a stack using a priority queue.
inputFormat:
First line contains the number of elements in stack,N.
Next line contains N elements in stack.
outputFormat: Pop all the elements from the stack and print them.

name: Implement A Stack (GetMin() in O(1))
description: Design a stack that supports GetMin() in O(1) time and O(1) extra space. GetMin() returns the minimum element in stack in O(1) time and space complexity.
inputFormat:
Fist line contains N, number of elements in stack.
Next line contains N elements of stack.
outputFormat: Print the Minimum element from stack.

name: Kartik Bhaiya And The Celebrity Problem
description:
Kartik  Bhaiya, mentor at Coding Blocks, organized a party for their interns at Coding Blocks. In a party of N people, only one person is known to everyone. Such a person may be present in the party, if yes, she/he doesn’t know anyone in the party. We can only ask questions like “does A know B? “.

Find the stranger (celebrity) in minimum number of questions.
inputFormat:
First line contains N, number of persons in party.
Next line contains the matrix of N x N which represents A knows B when it's value is one.
outputFormat: Print the celebrity ID which is between 0 and N-1. If celebrity is not present then print "No Celebrity".

name: Matched Brackets
description:
The nesting depth of a well-bracketed sequence tells us the maximum number of levels of inner matched brackets enclosed within outer matched brackets. For instance, the nesting depth of () and ()()() is 1, the nesting depth of (()) and ()(()) is 2, the nesting depth of ((())) is 3, and so on.

Given a well-bracketed sequence, we are interested in computing the following:

- The nesting depth, and the first position where it occurs–this will be the position of the first opening bracket at this nesting depth, where the positions are numbered starting with 1.

- The maximum number of symbols between any pair of matched brackets, including both the outer brackets, and the first position where this occurs–that is, the position of the first opening bracket of this segment

name: Triplet from three linked lists
description: Given three linked lists, say a, b and c, find one node from each list such that the sum of the values of the nodes is equal to a given number say, Target. As any number of answers can be possible return the first one you get while traversing.
constraints: The Size of the Lists can be different.
inputFormat:
The First Line contains 3 Integers n, m and k as the Size of the Three LinedLists.
Next 3 Lines contains n, m and k integers Respectively as the elements of Linked Lists.
Next Line contains the an Integer as Target.
outputFormat: Display the 3 elements from each of the Lists whose sum is equals to the target separated by space.

name: Flattening a Linked List
description:
Given a linked list where every node represents a linked list and contains two pointers of its type:
- Pointer to next node in the main list (we call it ‘right’ pointer in below code)
- Pointer to a linked list where this node is head (we call it ‘down’ pointer in below code).
- All linked lists are sorted.

Write a function flatten() to flatten the lists into a single linked list. The flattened linked list should also be sorted.
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N denoting the number of head nodes connected to each other.

Second line contains N space separated numbers (M1, M2...Mn) denoting number of elements in linked lists starting with each head.

Third line contains all the elements of the linked list starting with 1st head node and covering all the elements through its down pointer, then 2nd head node and covering all its elements through down pointer and so on till the last head node of the linked list.
outputFormat:
Changes must be done in the Original LinkedList so no necesaary to return head of the LinkedList.

Simply display the new LinkedList in a space separated manner.

name: Linked List - Fold
description:
Given a singly linked list: A0→A1→…→An-1→An,
reorder it to: A0→An→A1→An-1→A2→An-2→…

It is recommended do this in-place without altering the nodes' values.
inputFormat:
The First Line contains an Integer as the number of test cases.

Next Line contains an Integer N as the size of the Linked Lists.

Next Line contains N Integers separated by space.
outputFormat: print the Folded Linked-List for each test case separated by a new Line.

name: Power to Built
description:
Implement pow(x, n) % d.

In other words, given x, n and d,

find (xn % d)
constraints:
Note that remainders on division cannot be negative.

In other words, make sure the answer you return is non negative.
inputFormat:
The First Line contains an Integer T, for the number of test cases.
Next Line contains 3 Integers x, n and d separated by space.
outputFormat: Print the answer caculated for each test case separated by a new Line.

name: Largest Coprime Divisor
description:
You are given two positive numbers A and B. You need to find the maximum valued integer X such that:

X divides A i.e. A % X = 0
X and B are co-prime i.e. gcd(X, B) = 1
inputFormat: Two space separated integers A and B
outputFormat: Single Integer X where X divides A i.e. A % X = 0 X and B are co-prime i.e. gcd(X, B) = 1

name: Numerology And Ruby
description: There are several special numbers in numerology. One such number is the Ruby numbers. Ruby numbers are the one with no consecutive zero in them. Given 2 positive integer N and K find the total number of Ruby numbers that can be formed which only have N digits and the digits of the numbers lie in the set {0, 1, 2....K-1}.
inputFormat: The input contains two integers N and K
outputFormat: A single number denoting the total number of Ruby numbers that can be formed with the given N and K.

name: Ms Garima and PratapGarh Farms
description:
Ms Garima is an Mentor at Coding Blocks. She is Very Hardworking and Dedicated towards her work and She has successfully Completed her Winter Batch in which all of the students have Submitted the Assingment and were Satisfied with the Promises made before the batch. To relieve her mind after so much of work, She is thinking of a Tour to PratapGarh Farms with the TAs of her Batch. On route of PratapGarh Farms, There is a Circle Roundabout.

On the Circle there are N Petrol Pumps.
Suppose we have a App of the Circle due to which we have Two sets of Data,
- The amount of petrol that every petrol pump has.
- Distance from that petrol pump to the next petrol pump.

In order to Grab full of the Journey, She has given a task to the TAs and the Task is to find the first point from where the Car will be able to complete the circle (The Car will stop at each petrol pump and it has infinite capacity).

__Note__: Assume for 1 litre petrol, the Car can go 1 unit of distance.
On behalf of TAs Your job is to Submit the Solution of the given Problem Statement.
inputFormat: The first line will contain an integer N denoting the number of petrol pumps.  Next N lines are Two space separated values petrol and distance denoting the amount of petrol every petrol pump has and the distance to next petrol pump respectively .
outputFormat: The output of each test case will be the index of the the first point from where a Car will be able to complete the circle otherwise -1.

name: Rotten Mangoes
description:
Given a matrix of dimension m*n where each cell in the matrix can have values 0, 1 or 2 which has the following meaning:

   0: Empty cell
   1: Cells have fresh oranges
   2: Cells have rotten oranges

So we have to determine what is the minimum time required so that all the Mangoes become rotten. A rotten Mango at index [i,j] can rot other fresh Mango at indexes [i-1,j], [i+1,j], [i,j-1], [i,j+1] (up, down, left and right). If it is impossible to rot every Mango then simply return -1.
inputFormat: The first line of input contains an integer T denoting the number of test cases. Each test case contains two integers r and c, where r is the number of rows and c is the number of columns in the array a[]. Next r lines contains space separated c elements each in the array a[].
outputFormat: Print an integer which denotes the minimum time taken to rot all the Mangoes.(-1 if it is impossible).

name: Age Of Ultron
description:
Iron man and the rest of the avengers are fighting the army of ultron. Iron man regrets the fact that why he made ultron and now he wants to fight all of them alone. Army of ultron is spread across different cities from City of Sukovia to new york. Find the minimum money iron man needs to fight all the ultrons from the city of Sukovia to New York with multiple cities across.
As we know iron man is rich as hell so apart from his iron suit he uses money as the power to fight the ultrons .

1) He can either choose to pay all the ultrons of a particular city and escapes from there to the next city.
2) Or he can battle at the city by the army of ultron he has bought from other cities.
3) Or he can pay double the cost of a particular city and hire all the ultrons to his own army and move ahead.

RULES:

1) Iron man can choose to fight at a city if the number of hired ultrons is strictly greater than the count of all the ultrons at the respective city .
2) Each hired ultron can fight 3 times only .
3) For each battle iron man loose equal no of ultrons with him as well as available in the
city. Rest of the ultrons will lose 1 round battle irrespective of the fact that they are alive or not. After 3 fights they will not survive. If iron man has 10 ultrons in his army with him and total ultrons at a city , then iron man will lose 8 ultrons in the fight and remaining 2 will lost 1 round of battle and hence can be available for more 2 rounds only
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer n, denoting number of toll gates
 Next n lines contain 2 integers each, denoting number of men and cost of that toll gate.
outputFormat: Print the minimum cost

name: Ms Bhavana and The CB T-Shirt
description:
Coding Blocks has Decided to Design new T-shirt for beginner batches of C++ and java. Ms. Bhavana Mam is a Dedicated and Hard Working Member of Coding Blocks and She is the one who is Working on the new Design because of her Unique Taste.

She is thinking of using Binary Pattern on the T-Shirt. For the Binary Pattern She ask you to Write a Program to Generate Binary Numbers. Your job is to write a program that generates and prints all binary numbers with decimal values from 1 to n.
inputFormat: The first line of input contains an integer T denoting the number of test cases.  The first line of each test case is N.
outputFormat: Print all binary numbers with decimal values from 1 to n in a single line for each Test Case separated by a new Line.

name: FRED
description:
Fred is a student of class 10th. He likes to play with numbers. Recently he is busy in finding minimum number of steps that it would take to reach a number to one. He can only make following moves on the number.
A)	Subtract one from it.
B)	If it is divisible by 2, divide it by 2.
C)	If it is divisivle by 3, divide it by 3.
Just write the brute force recursive solution for this.
For example if we have input 10 then :
10 -1 = 9 /3 = 3 /3 = 1 ( 3 steps ).
inputFormat:
First line of input contains an ineteger T denoting the number of testcases.
Each of the next T lines contains positive integer 'n'.
outputFormat: single integer showing the minimum number of steps required

name: Recover Binary Search Tree
description:
Two elements of a binary search tree (BST) are swapped by mistake.
Tell us the 2 values swapping which the tree will be restored.
constraints:
1 <= n <= 10^5

Your recovery algorithm should work in O(n) time.
inputFormat:
First line contains n denoting the input size.

Next line contains n space separated integers denoting the preorder input of the tree.

NOTE : -1 indicates that the node does not exist.
outputFormat: Print the two integers in space separated manner. The output should be sorted.

name: Good Subarray
description: You are given two arrays A and B. An element of an array A is said to be good if it is present in a subarray of an array ( i.e. A[ai, ai+1,……, ai+l] {i<=x<=i+l} ) and there exists same subarray in array B (i.e. of same length and relative order of elements is also same).You need to find all the elements that are not good in array A.
constraints:
1<=N,M<=10^5.
-10^9 <= x <= 10^9 ( where x is the element of the array ).
inputFormat:
First line contains two integers N and M  denoting the size of the array A and B respectively.
Next two lines contains space separated integers denoting the elements of the array A and B respectively.
outputFormat: A single integer denoting the number of elements that are not good in array A.

name: Utkarsh Bhaiya and his busy routine
description:
Utkarsh bhaiya is very punctual. He never comes late to take the class. He lives at a very long distance from coding blocks Pitampura center so he has to get up early in the morning to get ready for the class. But last night he slept very late as he was watching a movie and when he woke up he was already too late.
He lives N steps away from the class. Coding blocks is at the step number 1. Now he has to reach CB asap. But he can only take auto, local bus or cab. He can also travel some distance using auto and then can take bus or cab ( or vice versa or any combination he wants ) . But he can only take one at a time and also if there is availability of the given transport that he wants to take.
If he takes auto then he can move one step in one time unit.
If he takes a local bus he can move directly to n/2th step in one time unit.
If he takes cab then he can move directly to n/3th step in one time unit.
But as I said he can take these transports only if they are available. Auto is available everywhere. Local bus is available only if n is divisible by 2. Cab is available only if n is divisible by 3. Now as he is already late you need to find the minimum time unit it will take to help reach Utkarsh sir coding blocks.
inputFormat: Single integer denoting the distance of Utkarsh sir’s home from CB.
outputFormat: Single integer – ( i. e. minimum time required ).

name: Playing with an integer
description:
You are given three integers A, B and D. You can perform three type of operations on D.You can perform these operations as many times as you want.
1.	You can add or subtract A from D.
2.	You can add or subtract B from D.
3.	Any combination of addition or subtraction of A and B on D.
Now you are given an array of numbers you have to find how many numbers are there in the array that can be formed by applying given operations on D.
constraints:
1 <= N <= 10^5
-10^9 <= X,A,B,D <= 10^9 ( X IS THE ELEMENT OF THE ARRAY )
inputFormat:
First line on input contains three integers A, B and D
Second line of input contains N (size of the array )
Third line of input contains N space separated integers
outputFormat: Single integer

name: Fred and Zola
description: Fred and Zola are two best friends. They always like playing with each other. Today they have a bucket full of balls. Each ball have some number written on it. Now they want to distribute balls among themselves. If there are n balls in the bucket then they will have n/2 each. If n is odd then one will have (n-1)/2 and other will have (n+1)/2. They want to distribute these balls in such a way that difference of  sum of numbers written on the balls that they have is as minimum as possible. Help Fred and Zola in this distribution.
inputFormat:
Fist line of input contains N the number of balls in the bucket.
Next line contains N space separated integers denoting numbers written on the ball.
outputFormat:
Numbers written on balls that Fred have.
Second line – output the numbers that Zola have.

name: Array and queries
description: You are given an array of integers. You will be asked M queries. In each query you will be given an integer X. You have to print the Xth largest element of the array for each query.
inputFormat:
First line of input contains an integer N denoting the size of the array.
Next line contains N space separated integers denoting the elements of the array.
Next line contains an integer M.
In next M line there will be single integer X
outputFormat: Print the Xth largest element of the array for each query.

name: Cubic Subsets
description:
You are given two sets of numbers A and B. You should find a subset A' of A and another subset B' of B such that:
- A' and B' are non-empty.
- For each element a in A' and each element b in B' , a * b is a perfect cube.
- |A'|^2+|B'|^2 is maximized (we denote by |A'| the number of elements of A', the same goes for |B'| ).
constraints:
1 ≤ T ≤ 10^4
1≤ N,M ≤ 5 ∗ 10^5
The sum of N + M for all the T tests is between 1 and 5 * 10^5.
The elements of A and B are integers between 1 and 10^6.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer T representing the number of test cases that will follow.
Each test case consists of three lines:
The first line contains two integer N and M, representing the size of A and the size of B, respectively.
The second line contains the N values of A.
The third line contains the M values of B.
outputFormat: Output T lines, each containing the answer for one test. If there is no solution, the line should contain −1, otherwise output the maximum possible value of |A'|^2+|B'|^2.

name: Samraj And Bits
description:
Samraj loves to play with numbers. Somebody gave him some numbers and he wishes to play a game with them. There are 3 operations that have to be applied periodically on the given set of numbers.

 The operations to be applied in periodic manner are (bitwise) XOR, ADD, (bitwise)OR.

Suppose there are five numbers. Then these operations will be applied in the following manner: ((((a XOR b) ADD c) OR d) XOR e). and it will go on further for more numbers in a periodic fashion.

You have to predict whether the maximum value possible by applying those operations cyclically from any chosen subset of numbers from the given set is odd or even.

 NOTE : The sequencing of the numbers in the subset will be preserved from the main set.
inputFormat:
The first line consists of an integer T. T testcases follow.
The first line of each testcase consists of an integer N.
In next N lines, each line will contain 1 integer denoting the elements of the array.
outputFormat: For each testcase, print the answer in a new line i.e. either "Odd" (without the quotes) or "Even" (without the quotes).

name: Suransh and Strings
description:
Prateek and Krishna are friends. Both of them like letters, especially upper-
case ones. 
They are cutting upper-case letters from newspapers, and each one of them has
their collection of letters stored in separate stacks. 
One beautiful day, Suransh visited Prateek and Krishna. He saw their
collections. Suransh wondered what is the lexicographically minimal string,
made of that two collections. He can take a letter from a collection when it is on
the top of the stack. 
Also, Suransh wants to use all the letters in the boys' collections.
constraints:
1 ≤ T ≤ 5
1 ≤ |A| ≤ 10^5
1 ≤ |B| ≤ 10^5
A and B contain only upper-case letters only
inputFormat:
The first line contains the number of test cases, T. 
Every next two lines have such format: the first line contains string A, and the
second line contains string B.
outputFormat: Output the lexicographically minimal string S for each test case in new line.

name: Cookies
description:
We all know that cookie is a culinary delicacy. While you were preparing for your birthday(and the after parties).So you ordered N types of cookies from the nearest bakery. For each different type you know 3 values:

- Ai = the time (in seconds) when the cookies of type i baked.
- Bi = the time (in seconds) then the cookies of type ii gets burned
- Ci = the quantity of cookies of type i

You also have M disposable cookie bags of large capacity (practically, infinite) and a microwave oven. As, of course, no one likes burned cookies, you wish to partition it in the M bags and then put those in the oven, setting a certain cooking time prepi such that in the end you'll have as much edible cookies as possible.

Formally, the cookies of type i used in bag j, which was cooked in the oven prepj seconds, is edible if and only if A i
​​ ≤ prepj
​​ ​i
​​ .

Given N types of cookies and the number of available bags, you have to find a convenient partition and the cooking times for each bag, such that in the end you'll have as much edible cookies as possible. Output the quantity of edible cookies.
constraints:
1 ≤ M ≤ N ≤ 10^5
1 ≤ A ≤ B ≤ 10^5
The total quantity of cookies doesn't exceed 10^9
Some bags can be left empty!
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers N and M.
Each of the next N lines contains 3 integers Ai, Bi,Ci , corresponding to each cookies type.
outputFormat: Output a single integer representing the maximum quantity of edible cookies you can get.

name: Partition on some Cost
description: You are given N segments on the x-axis. You should partition them in at most K sets. For each set, we define its cost as the length of the intersection of the segments in the set. Find the partition that maximizes the sum of the costs of all the sets.
constraints:
1 ≤ N ≤ 6000
1 ≤ K ≤ N
1 ≤ xi1 i2 ≤ 10^6 for every 1 ≤ i ≤ N
inputFormat:
The first line contains the two integers N and K.
Each of the following N lines contains two integers x1 and x2 representing the end points of a segment.
outputFormat: Output a single number representing the maximum sum of costs you can get.

name: RISHABH, RIYA , RAIN AND ROMANCE
description:
Now that Rishabh has proposed Riya after working so hard and packing efficiently Lobster Frittatas in Round 1 of Code like It Matters , they are successfully married now. They have planned to spend their honeymoon in Florence,Italy.After taking flight and having some rest , they both decided to visit a place where there are less people and the atmosphere is romantic and picturesque.

Unfortunately Riya is feeling thirsty suddenly and they have no bottled water with them.It’s a jungle and hardly you can get mineral water there.Suddenly there was a blessing in disguise as it started raining heavily.

Rishabh runs and collects some bamboo sticks to make a storage container and marked it with millimeter markings.
But since it was made in a hurry it had a leakage at height L millimeters.
If the water level is above the leak then water drains from the tube at a rate of K millimeters per hour (mm/h). Riya wants to figure out how much rain fell during a particular rainfall. Assume that the tube is high enough that it does not overflow. Also assume that rain falls at an (unknown) uniform rate during a rainfall, and that water does not evaporate from the tube. The height of the leak itself is also negligible.
constraints:
N<40
Each number L K T1 T2 H  is at least 0.01 and at most 1000.00, and each is given with two decimals.
inputFormat:
The first line of the input file contains an integer N  which denotes the total number of test
cases. The description of each test case is given below:
A line with five positive numbers: L K T1 T2 H where
 L is where the leak is (mm)
 K is the rate at which water leaks (mm/h)
T1 is the duration of the rainfall (h)
T2 is the time between the end of the rainfall and the observation of the water level (h)
H is the water level in the tube when we observe it (mm)
Each number is at least 0.01 and at most 1000.00, and each is given with two decimals.
outputFormat:
For each test case print one line with two floating point numbers F1 F2 where F1 is the smallest rainfall
in millimeters that would result in the given observation, and F2 is the largest rainfall in millimeters
that would result in the given observation.
You have to output till 4 decimal places.

name: RAJNEESH'S GREAT IDEA
description:
Rajneesh and Shradha are tired of the New Year tree, now they've got a new type of  New Year Tree at home!

A tree is a connected undirected graph where any two simple cycles have at most one common vertex. In other words, this graph doesn't have any edges that lie on more than one simple cycle.

On the 31st of December they are going to decorate the tree by hanging toys to its vertices. At most one toy is going to hang on each vertex — it's either the toy Rajneesh hung or the toy Shradha hung. It's possible for a vertex to have no toys.

Rajneesh and Shradha have been arguing, so they don't want any edge to connect two vertices where one vertex has Rajneesh's toy and the other vertex has Shradha's toy.

Rajneesh has decided to hang 'a' toys. What maximum number of toys 'b' can Shradha hang if they both cooperate to maximize this value? Your task is to write a program that finds the sought 'b' for all 'a' from 0 to the number of vertices on the New Year Tree.
inputFormat: The first line contains two integers n and m — the number of vertices and the number of edges, correspondingly. The next m lines contain two integers a, b each (1 ≤ a, b ≤ n, a ≠ b) that mean that there is an edge connecting vertices a и b. Any pair of vertices has at most one edge between them.
outputFormat: The first line must contain space-separated ba (for all 0 ≤ a ≤ n) where ba equals the maximum number of Shradha's toys on the tree considering that it has a Rajneesh's toys. Numbers ba go in the order of increasing a.

name: Swaroop's New Year Party
description:
Swaroop went to a Christmas party last night and is returning back home.On his way back he is listening to music. It takes 'k' minutes to reach home.Since he will be driving himself he will be playing his favourite playlist.After listening to the i-th song Swaroop gets a pleasure ai.The i-th song lasts for ti minutes.

Before starting his journey Swaroop turns on some song x and then listens to songs one be one i.e (x+1),(x+2) and so on.He keeps listening to songs till the end of playlist or he reaches his home.Swaroop can listen to each song completely or partly.Whenever he listens it partly he will be listening for integer number of minutes and at least half of the length of song.Mathematically if length of song is 'd' minutes Swaroop listens to it for no less than [d/2] minutes.Then he will immediately switch to next song if present in the playlist.For example if song length is 7 minutes he should listen to it for at least 4 minutes.If length is 10 minutes he must listen for at least 5 minutes.Take time taken to switch songs to be negligible.

Swaroop wants to listen partly no more than w songs. If the last listened song plays for less than half of its length, then Swaroop doesn't get pleasure from it and that song is not included to the list of partly listened songs. It is not allowed to skip songs. A pleasure from a song does not depend on the listening mode, for the i-th song this value equals ai.

Help Swaroop to choose such x and no more than w songs for partial listening to get the maximum pleasure.

Write a program to find the maximum pleasure Swaroop can get from the listening to the songs on his way to the work.
inputFormat:
The first line contains three integers n, w and k — the number of songs in the playlist, the number of songs Swaroop can listen to partly and time in minutes which Swaroop needs to reach home.

The second line contains n positive integers a1, a2, ..., an, where ai equals the pleasure Swaroop gets after listening to the i-th song.

The third line contains n positive integers t1, t2, ..., tn , where ti equals the length of the i-th song in minutes.
outputFormat: Print the maximum pleasure Swaroop can get after listening to the songs on the way to work.

name: HELPLESS HARSH
description:
Harsh is a very nice guy and has many friends. Two of his best friends Bablu and Yash have a habit of sending random FB messages to girls from Harsh's Facebook Id.But this time the girl on other side was annoyed and will accept Harsh's apology only when he solves the given below problem. You are a good friend of Harsh ,help him.

You are given a very simple task, lets call di be the number of digits in a-base representation of x.You need to find Σdi (i = 0 to x) for given x and a
inputFormat: First Line contains the Number of Test Cases, each containing 2 separated integers x and a
outputFormat: For each test case output a single integer, answer to the problem.

name: Product Sum for Every Window of size k
description: Given an integer N, we build an array A=[1,2,3,...,N]. For each subarray of length less than or equal to K, compute the product of the subarray's elements. Output the sum of these products, modulo M.
inputFormat: The first line contains three integers N, K and M.
outputFormat: Print the answer on the first line

name: Geek Geetanshu's Game
description:
Geetanshu always has the habit of doing something unusual.He is very geeky personality and this time he has developed a game of his own.
The game is as below. He will use N sheets of paper numbered from 0 to N-1.This game actually can be played only in dual mode i.e between two players only.At start N sheets can be assigned to Player 1 and Player 2 with equal probability but not necessarily equal number of sheets.

The game consists of a series of steps. In each step, a pair of sheets can be selected uniformly at random from all possible pairs that consist of two distinct sheets. The owner of the lower-numbered sheet will become the owner of both sheets in the pair. (If that player already owned both sheets, nothing changes, but it still counts as a step.)

The game ends as soon as all sheets are owned by the same player. Note that the game can end without any steps if all sheets are initially assigned to the same player.

This game is to be umpired by a third person. The third person has decided something for himself. Before the beginning of the game third player chooses a specific state, i.e., a specific way sheets are distributed between Player 1 and Player 2. At the beginning of the game and also after each step, if the current state is third person's chosen state, he eats a toffee.

You are given third person's chosen state as a String state. For each valid i, state[i] is either 'A' or 'B', indicating whether sheet i is owned by player 1 or player 2.

Geetanshu is  interested in the expected number of toffees third person will eat during a game. This number can always be written as p / q, where p and q are positive coprime integers. Let X be an integer such that X * q is congruent to p, modulo 1,000,000,007. Return the value (X mod 1,000,000,007).
inputFormat: The first line will consist of a string
outputFormat: Tell Geetanshu how many toffees third person will eat during the game

name: Minimize Semesters
description:
Mr. Dash has to study N courses numbered from 1 to N, but before studying each course Y Dash will has to study some another course X depicted by a dependency X->Y.
There are D such dependencies given to you.
There may be some courses which can be studied independently.
And also Dash is very intelligent so he can study more than one course per semester.
Now you have to find minimum how many semesters will be required by  Dash to complete all the N courses.

Note: i) relations[i][0] != relations[i][1].

ii) There is no repeated relations in the input.
inputFormat:
First line contains number of nodes n and no of edges e.

Second line contains u and v representing source and destination respectively.
outputFormat: Minimum  semesters required to complete all the N courses.

name: Intersection point of two linked lists
description:
Given two intersecting linked lists, write a function to find its point of intersection.  If the lists do not intersect , return NULL.

Note : You are required to only write a single function. Do not modify / alter the remaining code.

This is a stub problem so you need not worry about taking input or displaying output. Only focus on the designated function.
constraints: Your function should run in linear time.
inputFormat: You are given a function which accepts head pointers of two linked lists.
outputFormat: Return the intersection point node.
sampleInput:
Consider these linked lists :
1 -> 2 -> 3  -> null
   ↗
4

(This is not the actual input that will be provided but rather a description of it)
sampleOutput:
The two linked lists 1->2->3->null and 4->2->3-> null intersect at node with data 2.
Return the node with data = 2.

name: Weapon
description: In the climax scene of IT MOVIE , Bill the brother of Georgie has to make a choice when the clown was haunting them then he and his friends came to a place where they saw N number of doors through which they can get a weapon to fight with the clown. Each gate has only 1 weapon beside it. They have two choices either they can fight bare handed with the clown or they can open any number of gates and pick up the weapons beside those gates and then fight. The Task, You have to find the number of ways in which they can choose the weapons .
inputFormat: First line of the test case will be the number of test case T . Then T lines follows. On each line you will find a integer number N denoting the number of gates.
outputFormat: The output contains an integer in new line for each test case which depicts the number of ways to choose weapons to fight.

name: Strings With Benefits
description:
Strings are really cool and handy in use. To make the Problem more Interesting, For the Given Question we are going to take benefit of String and evaluate it in terms of some sort of Integer value.

Given a string of lowercase alphabets and a number k, the task is to print the minimum value of the string after removal of ‘k’ characters. The value of a string is defined as the sum of squares of the count of each distinct character.

__Note__: Must Try the O(n) Approach.
inputFormat: First line consists of T test cases.  First line of every test case consists of String s.  Second line of every test case consists of a integer K.
outputFormat: Single line output, Print the minimum square sum.

name: Sum of parts
description: You are given a integer **n** with no zeroes among its digits. You are asked to evaluate the sum of all formulas that can be generated by inserting '+' at positions in the string.
constraints:
T≤10

1≤n<10^11, n does not contain '0' digit.
inputFormat:
First line contains the number of test cases T.
For each test case, the line contains integer n.
outputFormat: For each test case, print the sum of formulas generated from n.

name: Empty the Basket
description:
Vikram needs to go to the market to buy some vegetables. However there are no empty baskets. He finds a basket with **M** marbles in it. Vikram is in a hurry, so he calls **n** of his friends to help him empty the basket.

His friends stand in a line, and in an orderly fashion, each grabs some marbles in their hand and carries it away. After replacing the marbles, they come back and rejoin the line at the back. Some of his friends are mischievious and instead of removing marbles from the basket, they put some marbles in instead. Let us consider that every friend takes one second to add or remove the marbles, and each friend can carry **ai** (1≤i≤n) marbles in his hands. That is, at any second, if the basket contains **m** marbles and the kth friend is at the front of the line, then at the end of that second the basket contains **m+ak** marbles.

How many seconds will it take to empty the basket?
inputFormat:
First line contains the number of test cases T.
For each test case, the first line contains two integers M and n.
The next line contains n space seperated integers, ai (1≤i≤n)
outputFormat: For each test case, print a single integer in a new line for the number of seconds to empty the basket. If the basket is never emptied, print "never".

name: Ragnarok And Quinjet
description: Thor made an escape plan from Sakaar Planet with Bruce Banner. He told Bruce that they will find the Quinjet and fly their way along to Asgard easily. But Banner told Thor that in order to fly Quinjet Thor has to solve a puzzle. Given a number A, Thor is supposed to find the count of numbers that are when added to A or Xored(Bitwise Xor) with A gives the same value. Thor is supposed to print the total count of such numbers.
inputFormat: A single integer, A
outputFormat: Print the total number of integers satisfying the criteria.

name: At Minimum Cost
description:
You have two strings, **S1** and **S2**, and you need to convert **S1** into **S2** by performing the following operations on **S1**:

i. insert a letter at any position (cost = **ci**)

ii. delete a letter at any position (cost = **cd**)

iii. replace a letter at any position with any other letter (cost = **cr**)

iv. exchange any two adjacent letters (cost = **ce**)

Find the minimum cost to achieve the conversion of **S1** into **S2**.
inputFormat:
First line contains the number of test cases T.
For each test case, the first line contains 4 integers ci,cd,cr and ce.
The next two lines contains the 2 strings S1 and S2 on seperate lines.
outputFormat: For each test case, print a single integer in a new line for the minimum cost of the conversion.

name: Kartik And Equation
description:
Kartik Bhaiya during his machine learning sessions encountered a mathematical equation which he is curious to solve. The equation is as follows -
(0tq0 + 1tq1 + 2tq2 + 3tq3 ............... + RtqR ) % C
 Consider 0 raised to power 0 as 1 here. Given the value of R, T, Q, C help Kartik bhaiya in order to solve this equation.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the number of test cases K.
Each of the next K lines contains four space-separated integers R, T, Q, C
outputFormat: For each test case output single integer, the value of the expression

name: Properly Painted
description:
A painter is painting a wall. It is in the form of a matrix of cells, with a rows and b columns. He moves the brush as follows: the 1st row, the 2nd row, and so on upto the ath row, then across the a-1th row, a-2th row upto the 1st row, then back to the 2nd row, and so on. The brush always moves across the row from left to right, i.e. from the 1st cell to the bth. The painter paints exactly n cells and then stops.

You notice that in this method the cells get uneven coatings. You set out to prove this.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the number of test cases.

The next T lines contain five integers: a, b, n, x and y.
outputFormat: For each test case print three integers: the maximum coatings on a cell, the minimum coatings on a cell and coatings on the cell of the xth row and yth column.

name: Perfect String
description: There is a string consisting of only ‘x’ and ‘y’ as the characters. Perfectness of a string is described as the maximum length substring of equal characters. You have given a number K which denotes the maximum number of characters that you can change. Find the maximum perfectness that you can generate by changing no more than K characters of the string.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer denoting the value of K.
The next line contains a string having only ‘x’ and ‘y’ as the characters.
outputFormat: A single integer denoting the maximum perfectness achievable.

name: Who will work?
description:
There are n workers in a factory with ids numbered from 1 to n.

They have to perform k jobs, the ith described by a tuple (ai, bi, ci): the starting and ending times of the jobs and the number of workers required by the job respectively.

For successfully completing the ith job you need ci workers working from time ai to bi inclusive. For doing the job, ci workers with the smallest ids will be chosen from all the free workers. If at the second ai there are not enough free workers, the job is unsuccessfull.
Determine the successfull jobs.
inputFormat:
The first line contains n and k.

The next k lines contain ai, bi, ci for the ith job.

ai will be distinct for each job and will appear in increasing order.
outputFormat:
Print k lines.

If the i-th task is unsuccessfull, print '-1', otherwise print the sum of workers ids who perform the task.

name: Maximal Arrangement
description:
Given an arrangement of the integers 1, 2, ..., x and a set of k pairs of indices (pj, qj), you have to find the maximal arrangement of these integers applying swaps only on the position specified by the pairs.

To understand maximal arrangement, let us consider arrangements of [1,2,3].
Then [3,2,1] > [3,1,2] > [2,3,1] > [2,1,3] > [1,3,2] > [1,2,3]. Here [3,2,1] is the maximal arrangement.
constraints:
1 ≤ x, k ≤ 10^5

1 ≤ ai ≤ x

1 ≤ pj, qj ≤ x
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers x and k.
The second line contains x distinct integers ai.
Each of the last k lines contains two integers (pj, qj) — the index pairs you can swap.
outputFormat: Print x integers - the maximal arrangement of the given x integers.

name: Count Anagrams
description: Given a string of lower alphabet characters, count total substring of this string which are anagram to each other.
inputFormat:
The First Line contains an Integer as Number of Test case.
Next Line contains String which is str.
outputFormat: Print the count of substrings for each test case separated by a new line.

name: Pretty Arrangements
description:
How many arrangements of length **n**, of integers **1** to **n** satisfy the condition, that **ai - i** is not equal to **p** for all **i** from **1** to **n**?
Since the number of arrangements may be very large, print the answer modulo 10^9+7.
inputFormat: The only line contains two integers n and p.
outputFormat: Print the number of valid arrangements.

name: Longest palindromic subsequence
description: Given a sequence, find the length of the longest palindromic subsequence in it. For example, if the given sequence is “BBABCBCAB”, then the output should be 7 as “BABCBAB” is the longest palindromic subseuqnce in it. “BBBBB” and “BBCBB” are also palindromic subsequences of the given sequence, but not the longest ones.
inputFormat: First line of each test case contains a string s .
outputFormat: Print an integer denoting the longest palindromic subsequence .

name: Anagram
description: You will be provided a string , you are supposed to count total number of substrings of this given string which are anagram to each other.
inputFormat: A single line input containing the input string
outputFormat: A single integer representing the anagrams

name: Cycle Detection and Removal in Linked List
description:
head - Head pointer of the Linked List

Return a boolean value indicating the presence of cycle

 If the cycle is present, modify the linked list to remove the cycle as well

complete this Method Given Below

bool floydCycleRemoval(Node head)
{
    /* Code here */
}

*   You do not need to refer or modify any code below this.
*   Only modify the above function definition.
*	Any modications to code below could lead to a 'Wrong Answer' verdict despite above code being correct.
*	You do not even need to read or know about the code below.

Given the head pointer to a linked list , complete the function to check whether there is a cycle present in the linked list. If so , modify the linked list to remove the cycle.

Note : You are only supposed to update the designated function. Do not change/alter the remaining code or your program may not work.
constraints: Your function should run in O(n) time.
inputFormat: Your function accepts one single argument that is the head pointer to the linked list.
outputFormat:
Your function should return a boolean value - True/False , indicating the presence of the cycle.

True if cycle is present, False otherwise.

If true , remove the cycle as well.
sampleOutput:
Your function should return True for the above linked list and remove the cycle as well
The new linked list should look like - 1->2->3->4->5-> NULL

name: The Tale of the Enchanted Scroll
description:
In the mystical kingdom of Palindoria, the royal library holds a magical scroll. Legends say that this scroll must always read the same forward and backward, or else the kingdom’s harmony will be disrupted.

One day, a scholar named Arin discovered that the scroll's text had been corrupted! Some letters were missing, making it not a palindrome anymore. To restore the kingdom’s peace, Arin must insert the fewest number of letters to make the scroll read the same in both directions.

Help Arin restore the scroll by determining the minimum number of insertions required to turn the given text into a perfect palindrome. You can insert letters anywhere in the string to achieve this.
constraints:
- 1 ≤ s.length ≤ 500
- s contains only lowercase English letters (a-z).
inputFormat: - A single string s consisting of lowercase English letters (a-z).
outputFormat: - An integer representing the minimum number of insertions required to make s a palindrome.

name: Minimum Spanning Tree
description:
Given an undirected weighted graph with V nodes and E edges , find the weight of the minimum spanning tree.
The IDs of the nodes are between 0 and n-1 inclusive.

Note : Try using both Kruskal and Prim's Algorithm for this problem
inputFormat:
First line contains two integers V and E.

Next E lines contain three space separated integers - u ,v and w

u and v are the nodes , w = weight of edge
outputFormat: Display a single integer denoting the total weight of the minimum spanning tree.

name: Can they meet?
description:
You are given a grid with **n** rows and **m** columns. Each of the numbers from **1** to **x** is present twice in the grid, at the coordinates **(ai,bi)** and **(ci,di)**.

You have to calculate if it is possible to draw curves that join the two pairs of coordinates for each of the numbers, in such a way that none of the curves overlap, or leave the boundaries of the grid.
constraints:
1 ≤ T ≤ 10

1 ≤ x  ≤ 10^5

0 ≤ ai, ci  ≤ n

0 ≤ bi, di  ≤ m

All points are distinct.
inputFormat:
The first line contains **T**, the number of test cases.

Then for each test case, the first line contains 3 integers, **n**, **m**, and **x**. The next n lines contain 4 integers **ai, bi,  ci and di** each, the coordinates of the two points where **i** is present.
outputFormat: Print **T** lines, each containing "YES" if it is possible or "NO" otherwise

name: Maximum Integer With At Most K Swaps
description: Given a positive integer, find maximum integer possible by doing at-most K swap operations on its digits.
inputFormat: Two positive integers N and K where N denotes the number on which swaps are supposed to be performed and K denotes the maximum swaps available.
outputFormat: Single Maximum integer possible by doing at-most K swap operations on digits of N

name: Generate Sorted Arrays
description: Given two sorted arrays A and B, generate all possible arrays such that first element is taken from A then from B then from A and so on in strictly increasing order till the arrays exhausted. The generated arrays should end with an element from B.
constraints:
Arrays A[] and B[] are Sorted.

2^A + 2^B <=10^9

A<=30

B<=30
inputFormat:
The First Line contains Two Integer N and M, as the size of both the Arrays.
Next Line contains N Integers separated by space as Array A[].
Next Line contains M Integers separated by space as Array B[].
outputFormat: Display the Sorted Arrays generated separated by a new Line.

name: Pattern-X
description: Print the following pattern.
inputFormat: N : Integer
outputFormat: Print the Pattern

name: Rotated Array
description:
Suppose a sorted array A is rotated at some pivot unknown to you beforehand.

Find the minimum element.

Given that the array will not contain duplicates.
constraints:
1 <= n <= 10^6
1 <= arr[i] <= 10^9  , where arr[i] is any element in the array
inputFormat: An integer n followed by an array A of size n.
outputFormat: Output should contain the minimum element in that array A.

name: Strange Road
description:
Rohan’s city can be represented as an infinite cartesian coordinate system. The City has a strange road system. It consists of a single road connecting all the points in the plane. The road starts from (0,0) and form the following pattern:-
(0,0) to (1,0), (1,0) to (1,1), (1,1) to (-1,1), (-1,1) to (-1,-1), (-1,-1) to (2,-1), (2-1) to (2,2) and so on. Rohan want to go from (0,0) to (X,Y).
Can you find the number of turns required to go from (0,0) to (X,Y) following the above described road?
inputFormat: First line of the input contains two integers X and Y.
outputFormat: Print a single integer representing number of turns required.

name: Road Construction
description: You are the construction planner of Delhi city. The city can be represented as a coordinate system. You are given the task to construct roads in the city but first you want to connect your house to your favorite restaurants. Your house is located at coordinate (X, Y). Coordinates of all your favorite restaurants is provided. If only straight roads can be constructed, what is the minimum number of roads required to connect all restaurants with your house?
inputFormat:
First line contains a single integer N representing the number of your favorite restaurants.
Second line of the input contains two integers X and Y, the coordinates of your house.
Next N lines contains two integers each, representing the coordinates of restaurants.
outputFormat: Print a single integer representing the minimum number of roads.

name: Smart Robber
description:
A professional robber planning to rob houses along a street. Each house has a certain amount of money stashed, the only constraint stopping him from robbing each of them is that adjacent houses have security system connected and it will automatically contact the police if two adjacent houses were broken into on the same night.

Given a list of non-negative integers representing the amount of money of each house, determine the maximum amount of money he can rob tonight without alerting the police.
inputFormat:
First line contains integer t as number of testcases.
Second line contains integer n as size of array.
Third line contains a single integer as element of array.
outputFormat: Print the maximum money  as output.

name: 3 Sum Closest
description:
For the coding blocks placement test , kartik bhaiya decided to give students an array arr of n integers and an integer target. The task is to return the sum of three integers in arr such that their sum is closest to target.

Assume that each input would have exactly one solution.
inputFormat: First line contains integer n as size of array. Second line contains the target .Next n lines contains a single integer as element of array.
outputFormat: Print the sum that is closest to the target.

name: K-reverse
description:
Implement kReverse(int k) i.e. you reverse first K elements then reverse next K elements
and join the linked list and so on.
3 → 4 → 5 → 2 → 6 → 1 → 9 for kreverse(3) becomes 5 → 4 → 3 → 1 → 6 → 2 → 9
inputFormat: Enter size N ,  N space separated elements and value of K ( no. of elements to be reversed)
outputFormat: Display the resulting Linked List

name: Cookies Piles
description: The kids in kindergarten made Christmas cookies with their teacher, and piled them up in columns.  They then arranged the columns so that the tops of the columns, going from shortest to tallest, were in a nice straight ramp.  The cookies were all of uniform size.  Given that there were A cookies in the shortest pile, that the difference in height between any two adjacent piles was D cookies, and that there were N piles, can you write a program to figure out how many cookies there were in total?
inputFormat: The first line contains the number of test cases T. T lines follow, one corresponding to each test case, containing 3 integers : N, A and D.
outputFormat: Output T lines, each line containing the required answer for the corresponding test case.

name: Party Halls
description: Given an array of meeting time intervals consisting of start and end times [[S1,E1],[S2,E2],...] (SI < EI), find the minimum number of party halls required.
inputFormat:
Take input N

Next N line  consists of two space-separated integers SI and EI
outputFormat: print minimum required room

name: K-reverse
description: Implement kReverse(int k) i.e. you reverse first K elements then reverse next K elements and join the linked list and so on. 3 → 4 → 5 → 2 → 6 → 1 → 9 for kreverse(3) becomes 5 → 4 → 3 → 1 → 6 → 2 → 9 → 1. If k is greater than the size of rest linked list then reverse the rest part. Ex. For linked list 5 → 4 → 3 → 1 and k =5. Output should be 1 → 3 → 4 → 5
inputFormat: Enter size N , N space separated elements and value of K ( no. of elements to be reversed)
outputFormat: Display the resulting Linked List

name: Sort linked list using merge sort
description: Given a linked list with n nodes. Sort the linked list using merge sort.
inputFormat: First line contains the number of nodes in the linked list n and then next line contains n space separated integers representing the node values of the linked list.
outputFormat: Print the linked list after sorting it using merge sort.

name: Non-Repeating character from a Stream
description: Given an input stream of N characters consisting only of lower case alphabets. The task is to find the first non repeating character, each time a character is inserted to the stream. If no non repeating element is found print -1.
inputFormat: The first line of input contains an integer T denoting the no of test cases. Then T test cases follow. Each test case contains an integer N denoting the size of the stream. Then in the next line are x characters which are inserted to the stream.
outputFormat: For each test case in a new line print the first non repeating elements separated by spaces present in the stream at every instinct when a character is added to the stream, if no such element is present print -1.
