if you go to date with crush, you cannot participate in the coding contest and you can’t watch the movie. Also if you play DotA, you can’t study for the exam. If you study for the exam you can’t sleep peacefully. The maximum number of activities that you can do for this schedule is 3.

Either you can

watch movie, play DotA and sleep peacefully (or)
date with crush, play DotA and sleep peacefully
inputFormat: The first line consists of an integer T, the number of test cases. For each test case the first line consists of an integer N, the number of activities. Then the next N lines contains two integers m and n, the start and end time of each activity.
outputFormat: For each test case find the maximum number of activities that you can do.

name: Pair of Topics
description:
The next lecture in a high school requires two topics to be discussed. The i-th topic is interesting by ai units for the teacher and by bi units for the students.

The pair of topics i and j such that (i good if ai+aj>bi+bj (i.e. it is more interesting for the teacher).

Your task is to find the number of good pairs of topics.
inputFormat:
First line takes an integers N(number of topics)

Next two lines, each following space separated N integers describing array a and b
outputFormat: Print the number of good pairs of topics

name: Subarray and Target
description:
Parie started learning DSA in Java. Today she completed arrays and decided to practice questions on arrays. So, she came across a question in which given an array of integers arr and an integer target, so she is supposed to print the total number of continuous subarrays whose sum equals to target.

But, However she is unable to solve the question, so your task is to help her in solving the question.
inputFormat:
An input integer n denoting size of input array.

n elements of input array

An integer k
outputFormat: The total number of continuous subarrays

name: All Divisions With the Highest Score of a Binary Array
description:
You are given a 0-indexed binary array nums of length n. nums can be divided at index i (where 0 <= i <= n) into two arrays (possibly empty) numsleft and numsright:

numsleft has all the elements of nums between index 0 and i - 1 (inclusive), while numsright has all the elements of nums between index i and n - 1 (inclusive).
If i == 0, numsleft is empty, while numsright has all the elements of nums.
If i == n, numsleft has all the elements of nums, while numsright is empty.
The division score of an index i is the sum of the number of 0's in numsleft and the number of 1's in numsright.

Return all distinct indices that have the highest possible division score. You may return the answer in any order.
constraints:
n == nums.length
1 5

nums[i] is either 0 or 1.
inputFormat:
You are given with  n the number of elements in an array.
n array elements.
outputFormat: Return the array.

name: Count Array Pairs Divisible by K
description:
Given a 0-indexed integer array nums of length n and an integer k, return the number of pairs (i, j) such that:

0 <= i < j <= n - 1 and
nums[i] * nums[j] is divisible by k.
inputFormat:
given an integer 'N'
n integers
integer k
outputFormat: Return the number of pairs of indices.

name: Reverse List
description: Write a program to print a list L in reverse order without creating a new list.
inputFormat: The first line contains space separated list items of list L.
outputFormat: Display a single line output of the list in reverse.

name: Henry wants binary systems
description:
King Henry VIII wants to break away from the catholic church. He has found an alternate for most of the catholic ways. Now finally he wants to change the decimal system.

Someone from his court suggests he should implement the binary number system. So he hands you the task of finding the number of 1s in each number in its binary form till a number N.

Given an integer n, Print an array ans of length n + 1 such that for each i (0 Note: It is very easy to come up with a solution with a runtime of O(n log n). Can you do it in linear time O(n) and possibly in a single pass?
Can you do it without using any built-in function (i.e., like __builtin_popcount in C++)?
inputFormat: First line takes an integer N(size of array)
outputFormat: Print an array ans, where each ans[i] is the number of 1's in the binary representation of i.

name: Flip bits
description: Given a binary array , find the maximum number of ones in an array with one flip of a subarray allowed. A flip operation switches all 0’s to 1’s and all 1’s to 0’s.
inputFormat:
First line of input contains integer n, denoting the size of the array.
Next line of input contains n space separated integers denoting the elements of the array.
outputFormat: Print the maximum number of ones in an array with one flip of a subarray.

name: Recycling
description:
You are a marketing head of a big MNC. You made a bar graph for your latest presentation. Now for your next project you need a rectangular sheet. But you don't want to waste anymore paper.

Since you don't need that bar graph anymore, you can use sheets from that. So, Given an array of integers heights representing the histogram's bar height where the width of each bar is 1, return the area of the largest rectangle in the histogram.
inputFormat:
First line takes integer N(no. of histogram bar).

Second line contains N integers representing the height of each bar respectively.
outputFormat: Print the largest area of the rectangle that can be formed in histogram.

name: Position of set bit
description: Given a number n having only one ‘1’ and all other ‘0’ in its binary representation, find the position of the only set bit. If there are more than 1 set bit then return -1. Position of the set bit ‘1’ should be counted starting with 1 from the LSB side in binary representation of the number.
inputFormat: First and only line of input contains single integer n.
outputFormat: Print the position of the only set bit, If there are  more than 1 set bit then print -1.

name: Monu bhaiya and Derangements
description:
Monu Bhaiya at the Beach. However, they decided to spend their time building sand castles.

At the end of the day, there were n castles built by friends. Castles are numbered from 1 to n, and the height of the ith castle is equal to hi. When friends were about to leave, Squidward noticed, that castles are not ordered by their height, and this looks ugly. Now friends are going to reorder the castles in a way to obtain that condition hi ≤ hi + 1 holds for all i from 1 to n - 1.

Squidward suggested the following process of sorting castles:

Castles are split into blocks — groups of consecutive castles. Therefore the block from i to j will include castles i, i + 1, ..., j. A block may consist of a single castle.
The partitioning is chosen in such a way that every castle is a part of exactly one block.
Each block is sorted independently from other blocks, that is the sequence hi, hi + 1, ..., hj becomes sorted.
The partitioning should satisfy the condition that after each block is sorted, the sequence hi becomes sorted too. This may always be achieved by saying that the whole sequence is a single block.
Even Patrick understands that increasing the number of blocks in partitioning will ease the sorting process. Now friends ask you to count the maximum possible number of blocks in a partitioning that satisfies all the above requirements.
constraints:
n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) — the

hi (1 ≤ hi ≤ 109). The i-th of these integers corresponds to the height of the i-th castle.
inputFormat:
The first line of the input contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) — the number of castles Spongebob, Patrick and Squidward made from sand during the day.

The next line contains n integers hi (1 ≤ hi ≤ 109). The i-th of these integers corresponds to the height of the i-th castle.
outputFormat: Print the maximum possible number of blocks in a valid partitioning.

name: Kartik Bhaiya wants to rotate a sorted array
description:
Help Kartik Bhaiya on this matter ASAP.
Suppose an array of length n sorted in ascending order is rotated between 1 and n times. For example, the array nums = [0,1,2,4,5,6,7] might become:

[4,5,6,7,0,1,2] if it was rotated 4 times.
[0,1,2,4,5,6,7] if it was rotated 7 times.
Notice that rotating an array [a[0], a[1], a[2], ..., a[n-1]] 1 time results in the array [a[n-1], a[0], a[1], a[2], ..., a[n-2]].

You must write an algorithm that runs in O(log n) time.
constraints:
n == nums.length
1 <= n <= 5000
-5000 <= nums[i] <= 5000
All the integers of nums are unique.
nums is sorted and rotated between 1 and n times.
inputFormat:
The First Line contains the input of N
The Second line contains the input of an array
outputFormat: Given the sorted rotated array nums of unique elements, return the minimum element of this array.

name: Elon Musk And Anagrams
description:
Elon Musk wants to find anagrams of a string help him to find the anagrams
Given two strings s and p, return an array of all the start indices of p's anagrams in s. You may return the answer in any order.

An Anagram is a word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of a different word or phrase, typically using all the original letters exactly once.
constraints:
1 <= s.length, p.length <= 3 * 104
s and p consist of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: The first line contains the input of string s and the second line contains the input of string p.
outputFormat: Refer to explanation

name: Check if a binary tree is height-balanced or not
description: Given a binary tree, determine if it is height-balanced. A binary tree is considered height-balanced if the height difference between the left and right subtrees of any node is at most 1.
constraints:
- The number of nodes in the tree is in the range: 1 ≤ n ≤ 105
- 1 ≤ Node.val ≤ 105
inputFormat:
- The input will be provided as a single line of space-separated integers representing the level-order traversal of the binary tree.
- Use -1 to represent a null node.
outputFormat:
Output true if the tree is height-balanced, otherwise output false.

Note: Do not modify or change anything inside the main function.

name: Reverse elements in Queue
description: You have to reverse the first k elements in the Queue.
constraints: Try to solve it in linear time.
inputFormat:
First line contains the N-the number of elements.
Second line contains the N elements.
Take input the value of K.
outputFormat: Print the queue after doing the above task.

name: Inorder Traversal
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return its inorder traversal as a list of node values.
constraints:
- The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 1000].
- -5000 ≤ Node.val ≤ 5000.
inputFormat:
- The binary tree is represented as an array in level-order traversal.
- Each integer represents a node's value.
- -1 indicates the absence of a node at a particular position.

For example, the input:

10 20 30 73 50 60 73

represents the binary tree:

        10
       /  \
     20    30
    /  \   /  \
  73   50 60  73

If the tree is incomplete, use null for missing nodes. For example:

10 20 30 73 -1 -1 73

represents the binary tree:

        10
       /  \
     20    30
    /        \
  73          73
outputFormat:
- A list of integers representing the inorder traversal of the binary tree.

Note: Do not modify or change anything inside the main function.

name: Monu Bhaiya going to Shimla
description:
Monu Bhaiya is going to Shimla. he has met two friends whose name is a strings m and n respectively. Check whether their name is an anagram if yes then print an array of all the start indices of n's anagrams in m. else print an empty list

Anagram means:
A word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of a different word or phrase, typically using all the original letters exactly once.
constraints:
1 <= m.length, n.length <= 3 * 10^4

m and n consist of lowercase alphabets.
inputFormat:
First line contains a string m.

Second line contains a string n.
outputFormat: A list containing integers separated by comma. e.g : [1,5,8]

name: Nokia Phone
description: Given a string containing digits from 2-9 inclusive, return all possible letter combinations that the number could represent.
inputFormat: You are given a string which has digits in it.
outputFormat: You have to print all the permutaion of the string.
sampleOutput:
ad
ae
af
bd
be
bf
cd
ce
cf

name: Time To Cheat
description:
You are a cheater. You cheat in all exams and tests.
Now that mid sems of your first year in college are finally here, you would like to cheat in these exams as well. You have the roll numbers of all the students in your class.

Now you want to know all the possible sitting arrangements of the students in your class.
Given an array arr of distinct integers, ie. the roll numbers of all the students of your class, print all the possible permutations.

Print all permutations in sorted order. Each line shows one possible permutation

Note: Please watch the Sample output once before submitting.
inputFormat:
First line takes an integer N (number of students in your class).

Second line contains N space separated integers (ie. the roll number of all students in your class).
outputFormat: Print all permutations in sorted order. Each line shows one possible permutation

name: Pascal’s Triangle
description:
You are given an integer N, return the first N rows of Pascal's triangle.
In Pascal's triangle, each number is the sum of the two numbers directly above it.
inputFormat: The first line of input is an integer N.
outputFormat: N rows of pascal triangle separated by a new line.

name: Domino Fall
description:
There are n dominoes in a line, and we place each domino vertically upright. In the beginning, we simultaneously push some of the dominoes either to the left or to the right.

After each second, each domino that is falling to the left pushes the adjacent domino on the left. Similarly, the dominoes falling to the right push their adjacent dominoes standing on the right.

When a vertical domino has dominoes falling on it from both sides, it stays still due to the balance of the forces.

For the purposes of this question, we will consider that a falling domino expends no additional force to a falling or already fallen domino.

You are given a string dominoes representing the initial state where:

dominoes[i] = 'L', if the ith domino has been pushed to the left,
dominoes[i] = 'R', if the ith domino has been pushed to the right, and
dominoes[i] = '.', if the ith domino has not been pushed.

Output a string representing the final state.
constraints:
n == dominoes.length

1 5

dominoes[i] is either 'L', 'R', or '.'.
inputFormat: A string denoting dominoes' configuration.
outputFormat: A string denoting the final state of dominoes.

name: Reveal Cards In Increasing Order
description:
You are given an integer array deck. There is a deck of cards where every card has a unique integer. The integer on the ith card is deck[i].

You can order the deck in any order you want. Initially, all the cards start face down (unrevealed) in one deck.

You will do the following steps repeatedly until all cards are revealed:

Take the top card of the deck, reveal it, and take it out of the deck.
If there are still cards in the deck then put the next top card of the deck at the bottom of the deck.
If there are still unrevealed cards, go back to step 1. Otherwise, stop.

Print an ordering of the deck that would reveal the cards in increasing order.

Note that the first entry in the answer is considered to be the top of the deck.
inputFormat:
First line takes an integer N(size of array)

Second line contains N integaers describing deck array.
outputFormat: Print an ordering of the deck that would reveal the cards in increasing order.

name: Journey Towards Numberville
description:
In the bustling town of Numberville, Mr. Block and Rajesh bhaiya had a puzzling challenge. They needed to find the kth smallest **distance between pairs of integers** in an array.

**The distance of a pair of integers a and b is defined as the absolute difference between a and b**.

Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the kth smallest distance among all the pairs nums[i] and nums[j] where 0 <= i < j < nums.length.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers N (the size of the array).and K
The second line contains N space-separated integers.
outputFormat: print the kth smallest distance

name: Decode Ways
description:
A message containing letters from A-Z can be encoded into numbers using the following mapping:

'A' -> "1",
'B' -> "2",
...
'Z' -> "26"
To decode an encoded message, all the digits must be grouped then mapped back into letters using the reverse of the mapping above (there may be multiple ways). For example, "11106" can be mapped into:

"AAJF" with the grouping (1 1 10 6)

"KJF" with the grouping (11 10 6)

Note that the grouping (1 11 06) is invalid because "06"
cannot be mapped into 'F' since "6" is different from "06".

Given a string s containing only digits, Print the number of ways to decode it.

Note: The output may exceed INT value so print output % (1e9 + 7)
constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 100

s contains only digits and may contain leading zero(s).
inputFormat: Each testcase takes an input string S.
outputFormat: Print the number of ways to decode it.

name: Phoenix and Socks
description:
To satisfy his love of matching socks, Phoenix has brought his n socks (n is even) to the sock store. Each of his socks has a color ci and is either a left sock or right sock.

Phoenix can pay one dollar to the sock store to either:

1. recolor a sock to any color c′ (1≤c′≤n)
2. turn a left sock into a right sock
3. turn a right sock into a left sock

The sock store may perform each of these changes any number of times. Note that the color of a left sock doesn't change when it turns into a right sock, and vice versa.

A matching pair of socks is a left and right sock with the same color. What is the minimum cost for Phoenix to make n/2 matching pairs? Each sock must be included in exactly one matching pair.
inputFormat:
The first line of each test case contains three integers n, l, and r  — the total number of socks, and the number of left and right socks, respectively.
The next line contains n integers ci— the colors of the socks. The first l socks are left socks, while the next r socks are right socks.
outputFormat: Print one integer — the minimum cost for Phoenix to make n/2 matching pairs. Each sock must be included in exactly one matching pair.

name: Minimum Operations to Make Array Unique
description:
Faraz hates duplicacy. On his 21st birthday Mayank wants to gift him a collection of integer numbers unaware of Faraz choices. Dhruv reminds Mayank that Faraz hates duplicates numbers. Now both are  trying to convert all numbers as unique by one operations many times.
* You can increment any number by 1 in one operation.

Help Dhruv and Mayank to find minimum operations to make all numbers unique
constraints:
1 <= total integer numbers  <= 10^5

0 <= Each integer Number <= 10^5
inputFormat:
First line take an integer N(total numbers Mayank has)

Second line contains N integers describing array all integer numbers
outputFormat: Print the minimum operations to make all numbers unique.

name: SPY Test
description:
This time you are appearing for the job of SPY. Adarsh is your interviewer. He has to take all applicants who solve his question soon. The question is as follow:

Given an integer array of even length arr, Print true if it is possible to reorder arr such that arr[2 * i + 1] = 2 * arr[2 * i] for every 0 <= i < len(arr) / 2, or false otherwise.

Solve this task soon to secure your position for next round.
inputFormat:
First line takes an integer N (size of array)

Second line contains N integers describing array.
outputFormat: Print YES if possible to reorder otherwise print NO.

name: CPU Tasks
description:
Given a characters array tasks, representing the tasks a CPU needs to do, where each letter represents a different task. Tasks could be done in any order. Each task is done in one unit of time. For each unit of time, the CPU could complete either one task or just be idle.

However, there is a non-negative integer K that represents the cooldown period between two same tasks (the same letter in the array), that is that there must be at least n units of time between any two same tasks.

Print the least number of units of times that the CPU will take to finish all the given tasks.
constraints:
1<=N<=10^4

0<=K<=100

task[i] is all upper case letter
inputFormat:
First line takes an integer N(size of array)
Second line contains N space separated char elements
outputFormat: Print the least number of units of times that the CPU will take to finish all the given tasks.
sampleOutput:
6 2
A A A B B B

name: Span Sum
description:
Alex is at the Central Library. The books there at the library are marked with a level depending upon the intended audience.

The span of a pile of books is the difference between the highest and lowest level book among the pile.

Find the sum of span for all the different possible piles of books in the library.
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N, denoting the number of books in the library.

Second line contains N space-separated positive integers, representing the level for the books.
outputFormat: Print the sum of all the span modulo 109 + 7.

name: Longest Arithmetic Subsequence
description:
Given an array arr of integers, Print the length of the longest arithmetic subsequence in arr.

Recall that a subsequence of an array arr is a list nums[i1], arr[i2], ..., arr[ik] with 0 <= i1 < i2 < ... < ik <= arr.length - 1, and that a sequence seq is arithmetic if seq[i+1] - seq[i] are all the same value (for 0 <= i < seq.length - 1).
inputFormat:
First line takes an integer N(size of array)

 Second Line contains N space separated integers describing array
outputFormat: Print the length of the longest arithmetic subsequence in arr

name: Max Area of Island
description:
You are given an m x n binary matrix grid. An island is a group of 1's (representing land) connected 4-directionally (horizontal or vertical.) You may assume all four edges of the grid are surrounded by water.

The area of an island is the number of cells with a value 1 in the island.

Print the maximum area of an island in grid. If there is no island, Print 0.
inputFormat:
First line takes integers N(no of rows) and M(no of column)
Next N lines each following M space separated integers describing grid matrix.
outputFormat: Print the maximum area of an island in grid

name: Tim’s Sort
description:
Tim has introduced a sorting technique to his peers, to efficiently sort a given list of numbers by dividing it into parts (sub-arrays), sort them individually and join (concatenate) them. The cost of sorting is inversely proportional to the number of parts, i.e., the more the parts of the array, the cheaper it is to sort.

You are given an array A, of size N, which consists of unique integers from [0, N – 1].
Find out the maximum number of parts the array could be divided into as per Tim’s sort, to give us the minimum cost.
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N, denoting the number of integers.

Next line contains N space separated integers, from the range [0, N-1], where each integer is unique.
outputFormat: Print the maximum number of division’s possible as per Tim’s sort for the given array.

name: The Sunday Lottery
description:
Vivek has bought a Lottery Ticket from The Sunday Lottery. The tickets have a number engraved on them.
 He has an insider tip, that greater the ticket number, higher the winning probability.

The Sunday Lottery also provides an option to their customers to change their Lottery Ticket, where they would swap any two digits of the ticket number and replace the existing ticket with the swapped one.

You are given a number representing the Lottery Ticket. What would be Vivek’s Ticket number, if he could use the option given by The Sunday Lottery based on the tip?

Note: He can use the option at most one time.
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer T, denoting the number of test cases.
Next T lines contain an integer, denoting the Lottery Number L.
outputFormat: Print the Ticket Number with highest win probability for each test case on a new line.

name: Cool Triplets
description:
You are given N tickets of different colors. The ith slip has an integer Ai embossed on it. Suppose we have a set of 3 tickets, with the numbers a, b, and c on it. This set of tickets is called a Cool Triplet if the sum of numbers on any two of them exceeds the number on the third.

Find out how many different Cool Triplets could be formed?

NOTE: Two triplets will be considered different even if one color forming the triplet occurs at different index. Expected Time Complexity should be less than O(n^3).
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N.

Second line contains N space separated integers.
outputFormat: Print the number of Cool Triplets.

name: Emily’s Birthday
description:
It's Emily’s birthday today, so all her friends brought candy for her. It’s customary at her school that every classmate of hers gives her one unique candy. Some of her classmates were absent on that day, so Emily’s best friend, being mischievous, snuck some extra candies in place of those friends into her Candy Bag.

You are given the contents of Emily’s Candy Bag, could you find which candies are from her best friend?
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N, the number of candies in Emily’s Bag.

Second line contains N space separated integers Ai, representing a candy from the person Ai.
outputFormat: Print the value that represents the candies from Emily’s best friend.

name: Estate Banking
description:
One weekday, Monu Bhaiya visits the nearby Estate Bank to get some transactions done. He happens to reach there just in time before the lunch break, however the clerk at the counter informs him that the Server’s down and no transactions could be processed at the moment.

He then visited the Bank the very next day as his transaction was due urgent. Not to his surprise, when he reached the bank, he came to know that all the upcoming transactions have been put on hold as the Branch Manager suspects that some duplicate tokens have been generated. Could you help the Bank find the duplicate tokens as Monu Bhaiya really needs his transaction done?

Try to find the duplicates in a single pass, using constant space.
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N.

Second line contains N space separated integers, denoting the token number.

Note: Every token is present either once or twice only.
outputFormat: In the order from left to right, print the duplicate token(s) as soon as it's repeated, on a new-line.

name: Keb's Particles
description:
Keb is an experimental physicist. His works primarily relate to the field of Subatomic particles.

Keb has set up a system which has N number of Z-particles. An array A, of size N is given where Ai is the charge on the ith particle. Find the effect on each of the Z-particles in the given system where  the effect on ith particle is the product of the charge of every other particle in the system.
constraints:
- 1 5

- |Ai| <= 100

- The product of any prefix or suffix of charge Particles is guaranteed to fit in a 64-bit integer.
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N.

Second line contains N space separated integers, denoting the charge Ai.
outputFormat: Print the effect on the particles of the system in a space-separated manner.

name: Linear Exams
description:
Linear Exams are coming and the Examination Cell has prepared a Question Set of N question papers. Each of the question papers belong to a set Si (1 ≤ i ≤ N).

There are M examinees seated in a row, and each of the examinee has a set Ti pre-assigned to them. The invigilator will pick M papers out of the N, and will give them one by one to the examinees, i.e. the first one he picks to the first student, the second paper to the second student and so on.

The invigilator believes that the consecutive papers have some similar problems in them, and so he decides to maximize the difference of positions of any two consecutive papers he picks up from the Question Set, help him find the maximum difference.

Note: You don’t have to maximize the difference among each of the M papers for the examinees, you only have to maximize the difference between the papers for any two examinees next to each other.
constraints:
2 ≤ M ≤ N ≤ 105

Si and Ti  are lowercase letters of the Latin Alphabet, where (1 ≤ i ≤ N)

It is guaranteed that the invigilator could always pick subsequent papers for the examinees from the given Question Set.
inputFormat:
The first input line contains two integers N and M — the number of question papers in the Question Set and the number of examinees.

The following line contains a string S of length N, the set of papers in Question Set.
The last line contains a string T of length M, the set assigned to a student.
outputFormat: Print a single integer — the maximum difference possible.

name: Interval Notation
description:
An array A, of size N is given. It consists of unique Whole numbers, in sorted order. You are tasked with representing the numbers using Interval Notation.

Print the smallest sorted list of ranges, such that the ranges must include only the numbers in the array. Each of the numbers would be included in only one of the ranges.
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N.

Second line contains N space separated integers.
outputFormat:
Print the list of ranges in sorted order, where each range is represented as follows on a new line,

For a range, [p,q]:

If p == q, print p

If p != q, print p->q

name: Limited Triplet
description:
Alex likes triplets a lot. His father recently gave him N integers, so Alex now wishes to find out that in how many ways could he make a Limited Triplet out of the integers.

A triplet of integers is a Limited Triplet, such that the absolute difference between any two of them doesn’t exceed K.

Note that the order of integers chosen doesn’t matter.
inputFormat: The first line contains two space-separated integers, N and K, and the next line contains N space-separated integers in strictly increasing order.
outputFormat: Print a single integer — the number of Limited Triplets.

name: Brittle Present
description:
Naved is turning 11 this weekend. His teacher awards him a problem every birthday and is expected for the same this year too. Naved is grown out of solving normal problems based on integers and strings, this year he wants a problem based parentheses.

A string formed by N characters ( or ) is said to be brittle if its length N is even and the first half characters are ( and its last half characters are ).

Naved is presented with a string formed of parentheses (not necessarily brittle). A step consists of choosing a subsequence of the string that forms a brittle string and removing all its characters from the presented string.
He has to perform the minimum possible number of steps on the string in such a way that no more operations are possible on the remaining string.

Since the given string is too large, Naved is unable to figure out how to minimize the number of steps. Can you help him do it?

A sequence of characters 𝑎 is a subsequence of a string b if a can be obtained from b by deletion of several (possibly, zero or all) characters.
inputFormat: The only line of input contains a string S consisting of only ( and ).
outputFormat:
In the first line print a single integer m, the minimum number of steps needed.

Then, print 2 × m lines describing the operations as :-

For each step, print a single integer k, the number of characters in the subsequence that is removed. On the next line print the k space-separated integers 1 ≤ a1 2 k, the position of characters removed in the step.

If there are multiple solutions, print the one including minimal positions.

All integers must be less than or equal to the length of the current string, and the corresponding subsequence must form a brittle string.

name: Bob at Wesley’s
description:
Bob is going to buy candies from Wesley’s Confectioneries. There are N candies placed in a row numbered from 1 to N from left to right. Each candy has a cost Ai , an integer.

Halloween is just around the weekend, Wesley’s are offering any candy for a discount if it costs strictly less than its neighbours. The leftmost and the rightmost aren’t free.

You can go to the shop before Bob and rearrange the candies. Find out the maximum number of candies Bob could get for a discount. Also, show how you would rearrange the candies.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N, the number of candies.

The next line contains N space-separated integers, A1 , A2 , . . . , AN, the prices of the candies reordered.
outputFormat:
In the first line print a single integer – the maximum number of candies Bob could have for free.

In the second line print the prices of candies as you would reorder them. If there are several orderings, print the one which costs Bob the least if he only buys the ones with discount and also place the cheapest at the leftmost possible position.

name: A Third Majority
description:
In yet another Number Line Election, Integers have come together to elect a representative amongst themselves. In contrast to normal elections, they have decided that anyone who secures more than one-third of the votes shall be declared a representative.

You are given a list of integers denoting a vote for that integer. Find the representative(s).
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N.

Second line contains N space separated integers.
outputFormat: Print the representatives on a newline.

name: Good Sequence
description: You are given an array A, of size N representing a sequence. The sequence is considered to be Good if no element is greater than its next. However, if you are allowed to modify at most one element. Would you be able to make the sequence Good?
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N.

Second line contains N space-separated integers.
outputFormat: “true” if the sequence can be Good, else “false”.

name: Polite Sort
description:
Dima has been assigned the task of arranging the books as per their identification number (an integer) on a shelf. She is very exhausted, so she asks one of her friends for help. Being polite she will only ask him to sort the shortest part (continuous) of the shelf such that if he only sorts all the books in that part, the whole shelf is sorted.

You are given an array A, of size N, where each element denotes the ID of the book on the shelf at that position. Find the minimum length of the shelf that Dima would ask his friend to sort to complete her task.
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N.

Second line contains N space-separated integers.
outputFormat: Single Integer, denoting the length of the shelf that needs sorting.

name: Library Impasse
description:
Monu Bhaiya is in a library. He approaches a shelf which has N books and each book has some amount of perks. Monu Bhaiya randomly chooses any book and decides to read all the books on its left or all the books on its right, depending on which side has minimum perks for all the books combined.

However, he reaches an impasse, if the perks for all the books together on either side are equal.

You are given an array A, of size N. Ai denotes the perk of a book. Print the index of the book for which Monu Bhaiya reaches an impasse.

Note: If there is no such index, then print “-1” and if there are multiple indices, print the leftmost index.
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N.

Second line contains N space-separated integers, representing the perks.
outputFormat: A number denoting the index of impasse, or -1 if no solution.

name: Festive Diwali
description:
This Diwali the Department of Culture & Heritage has decided to distribute sweets in each of the towns in the state. There are N different sweets prepared and are to be distributed to the N towns. Each town gets only one type of sweet and it is then distributed to all the citizens thereof.

You are given the sweetness of the sweets as A1 , A2 , … , AN and the number of citizens in each of the N towns as B1 , B2 , … , BN.

The festivity of the Diwali is represented by the sum of sweetness among all the people in the state, i.e. (A1 × B1) + (A2 × B2) + … + (AN × BN).

The Secretary of the Department of Culture & Heritage has assigned you to maximize the festivity this Diwali. Since all the preparations are already done, you aren’t allowed to re-order all the sweets to the towns, instead you can pick K {1 ≤ K ≤ N} sweets, Ai , Ai+1 , … , Ai+k-1 and reverse their order assigned to the towns.
Find out the maximum festivity possible.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N, the number of sweets and towns.

The second line contains N space-separated integers, the sweetness of the sweets, A1 , A2 , … , AN .

The third line also contains N space-separated integers, the population of the towns, B1 , B2 , … , BN.
outputFormat: Print single integer — maximum possible festivity possible.

name: Standing Problems
description:
Little girl Susie went shopping with her mom and she wondered how to improve service quality.

There are N people in the queue. For each person we know time ti needed to serve him. A person will be disappointed if the time he waits is more than the time needed to serve him. The time a person waits is the total time when all the people who stand in the queue in front of him are served. Susie thought that if we swap some people in the queue, then we can decrease the number of people who are disappointed.

Help Susie find out what is the maximum number of not disappointed people can be achieved by swapping people in the queue.
inputFormat:
The first line contains integer n .

The next line contains n integers ti  separated by spaces.
outputFormat: Print a single number — the maximum number of not disappointed people in the queue.

name: AAAAAAAAB
description:
Let's call a string good if its length is at least 2 and all of its characters are A except for the last character which is B. The good strings are AB,AAB,AAAB,…. Note that B is not a good string.

You are given an initially empty string s1.

You can perform the following operation any number of times:
- Choose any position of s1 and insert some good string in that position.

Given a string s2, can we turn s1 into s2 after some number of operations?
Note: It is guaranteed that s2 consists of only the characters A and B.
inputFormat: The first line of each test case contains a single string s2
outputFormat: Print "YES" (without quotes) if we can turn s1 into s2 after some number of operations, and "NO" (without quotes) otherwise.

name: Target Mayank
description:
Mayank needs some target money. He asks all his N friends to contribute. Each friend has a distinct  coin and he can contribute an unlimited number of that coin. Help Adarsh to find out how many unique ways he can collect coins from friends to achieve the target sum.

It is guaranteed that the number of unique combinations that sum up to target is less than 5550 combinations for the given input.
inputFormat:
First line contains integer N(no. of friends), target.

Second Line contains N distinct integers, representing the coin's value having each friend.
outputFormat: Print total number of unique ways Adarsh can collect money from friends which sum up to target value.

name: Chair Distance
description:
m chairs are arranged in a circle sequentially. The chairs are numbered from 0 to m−1. n people want to sit in these chairs. The i-th of them wants at least a[i] empty chairs both on his right and left side.

More formally, if the i-th person sits in the j-th chair, then no one else should sit in the following chairs: (j−a[i])modm, (j−a[i]+1) mod m, ... (j+a[i]−1) mod m, (j+a[i]) mod m.

Decide if it is possible to sit down for all of them, under the given limitations.
inputFormat:
The first line of each test case contains two integers n and m— the number of people and the number of chairs.

The next line contains n integers, a1, a2, ... an  — the minimum number of empty chairs, on both sides of the i-th person.
outputFormat: Print "YES" (without quotes) if it is possible for everyone to sit down and fulfil the restrictions, and "NO" (without quotes) otherwise.

name: Working Keyboard
description:
Recently Polycarp noticed that some of the buttons of his keyboard are malfunctioning. For simplicity, we assume that Polycarp's keyboard contains 26 buttons (one for each letter of the Latin alphabet). Each button is either working fine or malfunctioning.

To check which buttons need replacement, Polycarp pressed some buttons in sequence, and a string s appeared on the screen. When Polycarp presses a button with character c, one of the following events happened:

if the button was working correctly, a character c appeared at the end of the string Polycarp was typing;
if the button was malfunctioning, two characters c appeared at the end of the string.
For example, suppose the buttons corresponding to characters a and c are working correctly, and the button corresponding to b is malfunctioning. If Polycarp presses the buttons in the order a, b, a, c, a, b, a, then the string he is typing changes as follows: a → abb → abba → abbac → abbaca → abbacabb → abbacabba.

You are given a string s which appeared on the screen after Polycarp pressed some buttons. Help Polycarp to determine which buttons are working correctly for sure (that is, this string could not appear on the screen if any of these buttons was malfunctioning).

You may assume that the buttons don't start malfunctioning when Polycarp types the string: each button either works correctly throughout the whole process, or malfunctions throughout the whole process.
inputFormat: One single line takes a string as input
outputFormat: print one line containing a string res. The string res should contain all characters which correspond to buttons that work correctly in alphabetical order, without any separators or repetitions. If all buttons may malfunction, res should be empty.

name: Log Chopping
description:
There are n logs, the i-th log has a length of ai meters. Since chopping logs is tiring work, Adarsh and Tushar have decided to play a game.

Adarsh and Tushar will take turns chopping the logs with Adarsh chopping first. On his turn, the player will pick a log and chop it into 2 pieces. If the length of the chosen log is x, and the lengths of the resulting pieces are y and z, then y and z have to be positive integers, and x=y+z must hold. For example, you can chop a log of length 3 into logs of lengths 2 and 1, but not into logs of lengths 3 and 0, 2 and 2, or 1.5 and 1.5.

The player who is unable to make a chop will be the loser. Assuming that both Adarsh and Tushar play optimally, who will be the winner?
inputFormat:
The first line of each test case contains a single integer n — the number of logs.

The second line of each test case contains n integers a1,a2,…,an   — the lengths of the logs.
outputFormat: For each test case, print "Adarsh" if Adarsh wins or "Tushar" if Tushar wins. (Output without quotes).

name: Balanced Team
description:
You are a coach at your local university. There are n students under your supervision, the programming skill of the i-th student is ai.

You have to create a team for a new programming competition. As you know, the more students some team has the more probable its victory is! So you have to create a team with the maximum number of students. But you also know that a team should be balanced. It means that the programming skill of each pair of students in a created team should differ by no more than 5.

Your task is to report the maximum possible number of students in a balanced team
inputFormat:
The first line of the input contains one integer n (no. of students)

The second line of the input contains n integers a1,a2,…,an where ai is the programming skill of the i-th student.
outputFormat: Print the maximum possible number of students in a balanced team

name: Vasya and String
description:
High school student Vasya got a string of length n as a birthday present. This string consists of letters 'a' and 'b' only. Vasya denotes beauty of the string as the maximum length of a substring (consecutive subsequence) consisting of equal letters.

Vasya can change no more than k characters of the original string. What is the maximum beauty of the string he can achieve?
inputFormat:
The first line of the input contains two integers n and k ---the length of the string and the maximum number of characters to change.

The second line contains the string, consisting of letters 'a' and 'b' only.
outputFormat: Print the only integer — the maximum beauty of the string Vasya can achieve by changing no more than k characters.

name: Help Adarsh
description:
Adarsh is free at this time. He has a given array of integers arr, Now he is making all possible subarrays of this array and trying to find the sum of smallest element from each subarray.This process will take a long time so help him to find his result in less time.

Since the answer may be large, return the answer modulo 10^9 + 7.
inputFormat:
First line takes integer N(size of array) as input.

Second line contains N integers to the array.
outputFormat: Print the sum of the smallest element of each possible sub array.

name: Mussoorie Mountain
description:
John loves travelling.One day he had gone to mussoorie with Rashmi.While travelling they had visited an array of mountains having different peak points.When they had reached in the hotel they were willing to find the index of the Mountain peak point from the array of the peak points they had visited.Help them by returning the index of Mountain peak point from the array.

Mountain peak point means :
In the given array arr the Mountain peak point is arr[i] such that   arr[0]  arr[i + 1] > ... > arr[arr.length - 1].
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N.

Second line contains an array A having N peak points.
outputFormat: Single Integer, denoting the index of the Mountain peak point from the array A containing peak points.

name: Good String
description:
Let's call left cyclic shift of some string t1t2t3…tn−1tn as string t2t3…tn−1tnt1.

Analogically, let's call right cyclic shift of string t as string tn t1 t2 t3 …tn−1.

Let's say string t is good if its left cyclic shift is equal to its right cyclic shift.

You are given string s which consists of digits 0–9.

What is the minimum number of characters you need to erase from s to make it good?
inputFormat: Only one line contains string s.
outputFormat: Print the minimum number of characters you need to erase from s to make it good

name: Delete Two Elements
description:
Monocarp has got an array a consisting of n integers. Let's denote k as the mathematic mean of these elements (note that it's possible that k is not an integer).

The mathematic mean of an array of n elements is the sum of elements divided by the number of these elements (i. e. sum divided by n).

Monocarp wants to delete exactly two elements from a so that the mathematic mean of the remaining (n−2) elements is still equal to k.

Your task is to calculate the number of pairs of positions [i,j] (i<j) such that if the elements on these positions are deleted, the mathematic mean of (n−2) remaining elements is equal to k (that is, it is equal to the mathematic mean of n elements of the original array a).
inputFormat:
The first line contains one integer n — the number of elements in the array.

The second line contains a sequence of integers a1,a2,…,an, where ai is the i-th element of the array.
outputFormat: Print one integer — the number of pairs of positions [i,j] (i<j) such that if the elements on these positions are deleted, the mathematic mean of (n−2) remaining elements is equal to k (that is, it is equal to the mathematic mean of n elements of the original array a).

name: Reverse Linked List
description: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list, and return the reversed list.
constraints:
The number of nodes in the list is the range [0, 5000].

-5000 <= Node.val <= 5000
inputFormat:
N : number of nodes in a linked list.
Next line contains N numbers i.e. the value of n nodes.
outputFormat: Print the reverse linked list

name: Length of  longest substring without repeating characters
description: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
inputFormat: Input string
outputFormat: Length of longest substring with non repeating characters

name: Middle of the LL
description:
Given the head of a singly linked list, return the middle node of the linked list.

If there are two middle nodes, return the second middle node.
constraints:
The number of nodes in the list is in the range [1, 100].

1 <= Node.val <= 100
inputFormat:
first-line contains int n number of nodes
The next line contains n numbers
outputFormat: print the middle element of linked list

name: Mr. Block's & Array Puzzle
description:
There are n students in a classroom, each studying a Two subject. Teacher, Mr. Block scratches his head as he faces a puzzling challenge: he's given an array with a length of 2n, which represent marks of each subject for each student. His task is to shuffle it so that the sum of the first n elements isn't the same as that of the last n elements. Mr. Block is lazy. Can you crack this puzzle for him.To make this problem more interesting you have to find the lexicographically minimum rearrangement .

An array x is lexicographically smaller than an array y if in the first position where x and y differ xi<yi or if |x|<|y| and y is a prefix of x (where |x| denotes the size of the array x).
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer n(1≤n≤1000), where 2n is the number of elements in the array a.
The second line contains 2n space-separated integers  a1, a2, …, a2n (1≤ai≤10^6) — the elements of the array a.
outputFormat:
If there's no solution, print "-1" (without quotes). Otherwise, print a single line containing 2n space-separated integers. They must form a reordering of a.

Note : While Taking Input and Output Ignore Test case Input No and Test Case Output No,  These are for your understanding.

name: MATLAB Function
description:
Rohan started learning MATLAB and found that, there is a handy function called reshape which can reshape an M × N matrix into a new one with a different size R × C keeping its original data.
He was given an M × N matrix MAT and two integers R and C representing the number of rows and the number of columns of the wanted reshaped matrix.
The reshaped matrix should be filled with all the elements of the original matrix in the same row-traversing order as they were.

NOTE: If the reshape isn’t possible print the original matrix.
inputFormat:
First line contains two integers M and N.

Next M lines contain N space separated integers.

Last line contains two integers R and C.
outputFormat: Print each row on a new line with the values separated by a space.

name: Find the Word
description:
You are given a M × N grid of letters and a word, find out whether you can form the given word from the letters of sequentially adjacent cells of the grid. The adjacent cells are either horizontally neighbouring or vertically neighbouring.

NOTE: Same cell must not be used more than once.
inputFormat:
First line contains a string, i.e. word,

The next line contains two space-separated integers, M and N,

The following M lines contain N space-separated characters (letters) representing the grid.
outputFormat: Print true if the grid contains the word, otherwise print false.
sampleInput:
SEE
3 4
A B C E
S F C S
A D E E

name: Corners
description:
Corners is a game played in Eastern states of India.

It’s usually played with 4 or more players, where each player occupies a spot, representing corners of a polygon. A player who’s chosen to be the Tat must go to a player at one of the corners, who will then redirect him/her to one of the other corners. While the Tat is on his/her way to the redirected corner, others try to exchange their spot and Tat would try to take it as an opportunity to capture the corner, leaving one of the others as the new Tat, similar to Musical Chairs.

Mili was one day playing Corners with her friends, and a thought struck her mind. If all the players holding the corners make up their mind, and have decided where to redirect the Tat, then it may be possible that the Tat is stuck in a loop (or cycle) indefinitely.

Find the loop having the maximum number of corners.

Note: A player may redirect the Tat to himself/herself, representing a loop involving a single corner.
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N, denoting the number of corners.

Next line contains N space separated integers, from the range [0, N-1], where each integer represents the index (or position), where that player would redirect the Tat.

Note: Each value is unique.
outputFormat: Print the number of corners in the longest loop.

name: Solve Puzzle
description:
"Can you Solve this Puzzle : "

Given two sorted arrays of size m and n, find the median of these two sorted arrays in logarithmic time.
inputFormat:
First-line contains two integers n and m size of two arrays

Second-line contains the n element of array1
Third and last line contains m element of array2
outputFormat: A double value representing the median of the arrays a and b.

name: Mili's Gallery
description:
Mili has recently been assigned to get an old Art Gallery up and running. She was looking around for improvements needed to be done and found out there a too few paintings and artifacts. She wishes to add K more articles to the Gallery. However, for a better view, she wouldn’t place any two articles adjacently.

You are provided with an array A, of size N containing 0’s and 1’s representing the presence of an article the wall, where 0 means the spot is empty and 1 means the spot already has an article. Will Mili be able to add K more article without any two of them being placed adjacent.
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N.

Second line contains N space-separated integers, 0’s and 1’s.

Third line contains K.
outputFormat: Print “true” if its possible to add K more articles, without any of them being adjacent, else print “false”.

name: Maximize Earning
description:
You are given an integer array nums. You want to maximize the earning you get by performing the following operation any number of times:

- Pick any nums[i] and delete it to earn nums[i] points.
- Afterwards, you must delete every element equal to nums[i] - 1 and every element equal to nums[i] + 1.

Return the maximum earning you can earn by applying the above operation some number of times.
inputFormat:
First line of input contains an integer n represents the size of the nums array.
Following n lines contains an integer element of nums array.
outputFormat: Return the maximum earnings.

name: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List
description: Given the head of a sorted linked list, delete all duplicates such that each element appears only once. Return the linked list sorted as well.
constraints:
The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 300].

-100 <= Node.val <= 100

The list is guaranteed to be sorted in ascending order.
inputFormat:
Int n, number of nodes in a linked list

n numbers having values of n  different nodes
outputFormat: Print the updated list

name: Pastries in Hawen
description:
In the town of Hawen, there are N shops that sell Pastries. Each shop sells pastries with different amounts of taste. Dhruv wants to have pastries summing to K amount of taste. However, he would only have pastries from shops in a row one after the other i.e if there are 5 shops numbered 1,2,3,4,5 then eating from 1-3-4 would not be a valid choice whereas eating from 1-2-3 or 3-4-5 or 1-2 or 2-3-4-5 would be.

Could you find out the number of different groups of shops Dhruv could have pastries at?
inputFormat:
First line contains two space-separated integers N and K.
Next line contains N space separated integers, denoting the taste at the ith shop.
outputFormat: Print the number of different groups of shops Dhruv could have pastries at.

name: Largest Special Subset
description:
Given a set of distinct positive integers nums.

Return the largest subset answer such that every pair (result[i], result[j]) of elements in this subset satisfies a special property:

- result[i] % result[j] == 0, or

- result[j] % result[i] == 0

If there are multiple solutions, return lexicographically smallest.
constraints:
- 1 <= nums.length <= 1000

- 1 <= nums[i] <= 2 * 10^9

- All the integers in nums are unique.
inputFormat:
First line of input contains an integer n represents the size of the nums array.
Following n lines contains an integer element of nums array.
outputFormat: Print the lexicographically smallest answer array.

name: K-subarry
description:
Samwell tarley is a bit weak at finding maximum sub-array sum. So he asked you to find this for him. But the task is a bit new. The array will be fomred by repeating the array k times and then find the ans.

Note : As the answer can be very large, return the answer modulo 109 + 7 and length of the sub-array can be 0 and its sum in that case is 0.
inputFormat:
First Line would be length of array and k.
Secind line would be array elements.
outputFormat: The maximum subbary sum.

name: Save Princess
description:
The princess of Winterfell is trapped in grid in king's landing. His brother John came to save him. The princess is at the bottom-right corner of the grid. John does not have enough health but have to save his sister. While going throw the cells some cells have soldiers(negative numbers) his health would decrease fighting them in it while some have energy potions(positive numbers). He need to save the queen.

So your task is to find what is the min. health John should have in starting to save his princess.

Given that he can only move right and down and when his health become zero he will die.
constraints:
m == grid.length

n ==  grid[i].length

1 <= m, n <= 200

-1000 <= grid[i][j] <= 1000
inputFormat:
Two integers m and n denoting rows and columns.
Next m lines will have n integers to form grid.
outputFormat: Return the john'sminimum initial health so that he can rescue the princess.

name: Ambulances in Autille
description:
The city of Autille is divided into N blocks one after the other from East to West. The Healthcare authorities are working on improving the response time of ambulances in case of emergency.

There are K ambulances, the ith ambulance is stationed in the block Ai. No two ambulances are stationed in the same block(i.e. all Ai are distinct).

Each ambulance has a response time associated with it, the ith ambulance has a response time of Ti. The response time for any block is calculated as the minimum response time among all the ambulances, increased by its distance from the block.

For each block i, the response time would be,
min1 ≤ j ≤ K  (Tj + |Aj – i |)

Find out the minimum response times for all the blocks in Autille.
inputFormat:
The first line of input contains two space-separated integers, N the number of blocks and K the number of ambulances.

The second line contains K space-separated integers, A1 , A2 , . . . , AK , the blocks where the ambulances are stationed.

The third line contains K space-separated integers, T1 , T2 , . . . , TK , the response times of the ambulances.
outputFormat: Print N space-separated integers in a single line — the response time in each of the blocks.

name: Chitkara ST-3 Web
description:
Create a To-Do List using HTML,CSS and JS  as shown in the video.
You can also use jQuery to create this functionality.

Your To-Do List must  have the following functionalities.

1. Create To-Do item

2. Delete To-Do item

3.Move To-Do item Upward using up arrow button

4.Move To-Do item Downward using down arrow button

The colors or shape sizes may not be the exact same as in the video but your final page should look similar to what is given.

You have to submit your assignment through the google form.

**The link to the google form is**: Click For Link, In case click doesn't work you can copy paste this in your browser: https://forms.gle/GqjV5fSyCRctYmDK6
**Important Note -** Do **not** upload the HTML and CSS files directly. Put both the files together in a folder. Zip/Compress that folder and upload the zip file on the form.

name: Coin Change Problem
description: Given an unlimited supply of coins of given denominations, find total number of distinct ways to get the desired change.
inputFormat:
An input integer n representing size of set S.
n elements of S.
an integer representing desired change
outputFormat: Total number of ways to get a change

name: Longest Increasing Subsequence using LCS
description: Find a subsequence of a given sequence in which the subsequence's elements are in sorted order, lowest to highest, and in which the subsequence is not necessarily contiguous or unique.
inputFormat:
Integer n representing size of the array

n array elements.
outputFormat: Length of longest increasing subsequence

name: Truncate a binary tree to remove nodes that lie on a path having a sum less than `k`
description:
A complete path in a binary tree is defined as a path from the root to leaf. The sum of all nodes on that path is defined as the sum of that path.
Given a binary tree and a number k, remove nodes from the tree which lie on an complete path having a sum less than k.
inputFormat: Level Order traversal where -1 means child is NULL
outputFormat: Inorder traversal of the resultant tree

name: Nearest Leaf
description:
Given a level-order traversal of a Binary Tree, create the tree and find its distance from root to the nearest leaf node or the minimum depth. The distance to the nearest leaf is the number of nodes along the shortest path from root down to the nearest leaf node.

A leaf node is no node with no children.
inputFormat:
The only line of input contains space-separated values i.e. either an integer or N denoting the values of the nodes in level-order.

N denotes a NULL node.
outputFormat: Single integer – denoting the distance of the nearest leaf node.

name: Column-wise(Vertical Order) Traversal of a Binary Tree
description: You are given the root of a binary tree represented as a list in level-order traversal format. Perform a vertical order traversal of the tree.
constraints:
- The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 1000].
- Node values are integers in the range [0, 1000].
- Input must represent a valid binary tree in level-order traversal format.
inputFormat:
The program accepts input in the form of a level-order traversal of a binary tree as a single line of space-separated integers:

- Use -1 to represent null (for missing nodes).
- The input must be provided in level-order traversal format, where:
- The first number is the root node.
- Subsequent numbers represent the left and right children of the nodes at each level.
- If a node is -1, its children are skipped.
outputFormat:
The output is the vertical order traversal of the binary tree as multiple lines of space-separated integers:

- Each line corresponds to one vertical column in the binary tree.
- Columns are printed from left to right.
- Values within a column are sorted:
- Top-to-bottom order (based on row index).
- If two nodes are in the same row and column, they are sorted by their values in ascending order.

Note: Do not modify or change anything inside the main function.

name: 0-1 Knapsack Problem
description:
In this problem, you are given a set of items, each with a weight and a value, and we need to determine the number of each item to include in a collection so that the total weight is less than or equal to a given limit and the total value is as large as possible.

An array representing value of ith item.
An array representing weight of ith item.

name: Check Subsequence

Given two strings s and t, return true if s is a subsequence of t, or false otherwise.

name: Ice cream

After eating to his stomach's limit, Lakshya bhaiya realized that he forgot to eat dessert. Help Lakshya bhaiya select the lightest dessert !!

name: Selecting from Players Inventory
description:
In a multiplayer role-playing game (RPG), players have an inventory that can hold items such as weapons, potions, and tools. The inventory is represented as an array where each position holds a specific item. During gameplay, players can rotate their inventory to bring the next item to the first position for quick access.

To implement this feature, you need to write a program that rotates the inventory array by a specified number of positions in a clockwise direction.

You are tasked with designing a function to simulate the inventory rotation for players in the game.
inputFormat:
The first line contains a positive integer N and K.

The next line contains N space separated integer.(inventory array )
outputFormat: Print the resulting array.

name: 1D to 2D
description: You are given a 1D integer array of size N, convert it into a 2D integer matrix of the given dimensions, ie. a matrix of x rows and y columns.
constraints:
0 < N < 50000

N is the product of X and Y

N space separated integers.
outputFormat: X rows of Y integers each.

name: Blessing of Lord Shiva
description: Martin is a devotee of Lord Shiva. Upon noticing his good deeds and austerity, Lord Shiva asked Martin to make a wish and He will make that true but for that Martin was required to prove his knowledge. So, Lord Shiva gave him a binary string of a's and b's and asked him to make this string a sequence of alternate characters by flipping minimum number of characters possible. Now, its your duty to help Martin.
inputFormat: The first line of input contains a single integer T denoting the number of test cases. Then T test cases follow. Each test case consists of one line. The line contains a string of a's and b's.
outputFormat: Minimum number of characters to be removed to make string alternate.

name: Brick Wall
description:
There is a rectangular brick wall in front of you with n rows of bricks. The ith row has some number of bricks each of the same height (i.e., one unit) but they can be of different widths. The total width of each row is the same.

Draw a vertical line from the top to the bottom and cross the least bricks. If your line goes through the edge of a brick, then the brick is not considered as crossed. You cannot draw a line just along one of the two vertical edges of the wall, in which case the line will obviously cross no bricks.

Given the 2D array wall that contains the information about the wall, return the minimum number of crossed bricks after drawing such a vertical line.
constraints:
n == wall.length

1 <= n <= 10^4

1 <= wall[i].length <= 10^4

1 <= sum(wall[i].length) <= 2 * 10^4

sum(wall[i]) is the same for each row i.

1 <= wall[i][j] <= 2^31 - 1
inputFormat:
An integer n representing number of rows in the wall

Next n lines contains p and list of integers representing width of p bricks in ith row.
outputFormat: Minimum number of crossed bricks after drawing such a vertical line.

name: Chess Knight Problem | Find the shortest path from source to destination

Given a chessboard, find the shortest distance (minimum number of steps) taken by a knight to reach a given destination from a given source.

   This page contains a search box through which user can search multiple TV shows using TV Maze API (https://www.tvmaze.com/api).

   1.2 Add to favourites button will add TV show to the favourite list.

2.  Favourites page

 This page contains all the shows that you marked favourite. You can also remove favourites by clicking on the heart on icon on this page.

3. Details page

name: Sort array by set bits
description:
Given an integer array, you have to sort the integers in the array in ascending order by the number of 1’s in their binary representation and in case of two or more integers have the same number of 1’s you have to sort them in ascending order.

name: Palindrome Function
description: Write function which returns a boolean, indicating if the input S is a palindrome or not.

name: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
description:
Given a binary search tree (BST), find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) node of two given nodes in the BST.

According to the definition of LCA on Wikipedia: “The lowest common ancestor is defined between two nodes p and q as the lowest node in T that has both p and q as descendants (where we allow a node to be a descendant of itself).”
constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [2, 105].

-109 9

All Node.val are unique.

p != q

p and q will exist in the BST
inputFormat: Enter the number of nodes N and add N more numbers to the BST, then add the two numbers whose LCA is to be found.

name: Sliding Window Maximum
