- The second line contains n space-separated integers representing the array.
outputFormat: Output a single line containing n - k + 1 space-separated integers, where each integer is the maximum value of the sliding window at that position.

name: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
description:
You have a given sorted array of length N consisting of unique elements. Now your teacher rotates it for K times.
Notice that rotating an array [a[0], a[1], a[2], ..., a[n-1]] 3 times results in the array [a[n-3],a[n-2],a[n-1], a[0], a[1], a[2], ..., a[n-4]].

For example, an array nums = [0,1,2,4,5,6,7] might become:

* [4,5,6,7,0,1,2] if it was rotated K=4 times.
* [0,1,2,4,5,6,7] if it was rotated K=0 times.
* [7,0,1,2,4,5,6] if it was rotated K=8 times

You have this rotated sorted array now.Find the minimum element of this array.You must write an algorithm that runs in O(log n) time.
inputFormat:
Take an input N(size of array).

 Next line takes N elements.
outputFormat: Find the minimum element in this array.

name: Find Peak Element I
description:
Given an integer array arr, find a peak element, and return its index.

A peak element is an element that is strictly greater than its neighbors. First element and last element of the array can't be peak elements.It is guaranteed that there is at most one peak element and no local minima.

You must write an algorithm that runs in O(log n) time.
inputFormat:
First line takes integer N(size of array) as input

Second line contains N space separated integers of the array a0,a1,a2,....an-1.
outputFormat: Print the index of peak element if found otherwise Print “No Peak Element”without quotes.

name: Trapping Rain Water
description: Tushar is a rain harvester.He has a set of N bars with each bar of some height and width of 1 units.Compute how much water it can trap after next raining.
inputFormat:
First line takes integer N(no. of bars) as input.

Second line takes N integers defining the height of each bar respectively.
outputFormat: Print how much water is contained by this set of bars in the next rain.

name: Sri and Shopkeeper
description:
Sridharan is a chocolate lover. He went to the shop, there was an array of integers containing the number of chocolate in each index. Sri needs multiple of K chocolates. Shopkeeper agreed to give all subarrays which chocolates sum divisible by K.

Find the total number of ways Sridharan can take chocolates.
i.e Print the number of non-empty subarrays that have a sum divisible by k.
inputFormat:
First Line contains input N(size of array) and K.

Second line contains N integers where each integer is the number of chocolates present in that index in the array.
outputFormat:
Print the total number of ways Sri can take chocolates.
Note: arr[i]<0 means Sri has to give arr[i] chocolates to the shopkeeper.

name: Local Maxima
description:
You may have studied about Local Maxima when working with Functions and its graph on the Cartesian Plane. A Local Maxima is defined here as a point on the graph whose value is strictly greater than its neighbors.

You are given an array A, of size N. Find the position of Local Maxima among the given values.

NOTE: The first and last element need only be compared to the element next and prior to them respectively.

Try to find the local maxima in O(log N) time.
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N.
Second line contains N space separated integers.
outputFormat: Print the index of the Local Maxima.

name: Newbie Stock Trader
description:
The prices of a given stock on a day is given in the form of an array A, of size N. Where Ai is the price of the stock on ith day. Monu has just started trading in stocks and so he relies on one of his friends for advice.

His friend, for some reason, advises him to trade only on days where the price of the stock keeps rising every day. Would you be able to find the maximum number of continuous days where Monu can trade as per his friend’s advice?

Note: The price must rise daily for Monu to trade.
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N.

Second line contains N space-separated integers.
outputFormat: Single Integer, denoting the maximum number of days where Vivek can trade.

name: Zero Zero Sum
description:
You are given an array A of size N, and you are required to solve a task.

We would call a non-empty array nice if for every non-empty subarray of this array, the sum of elements is non-zero.

Calculate the number of non-empty nice subarrays of the given array A.

An array C is a subarray of an array B if C can be obtained from B by deletion of several (possibly, zero or all) elements from the beginning and several (possibly, zero or all) elements from the end.
inputFormat:
The first line of the input contains a single integer N  — the length of array A.

The second line of the input contains N integers A1 , A2 , . . . , AN — the elements of A.
outputFormat: Print a single integer — the number of non-empty nice subarrays in A.

name: Balanced Palindrome
description:
Divya has an array A, consisting of N integers. All the elements do not exceed some integer K.

She has posed herself with the challenge of making all the such pairs Ai and Aj sum up to a value, say X, where i is from 1 to N⁄2 and j = N – i +1. X should be the same for all the N⁄2 pairs. In order to do so, she would go on replacing the elements of A with a positive integer not greater than K.

Could you find out the minimum number of elements she would have to replace in order to work out her challenge?
constraints:
2 ≤ N ≤ 2 * 105

1 ≤ K ≤ 2 * 105

1 ≤ Ai ≤ K

N is even (i.e., divisible by 2)
inputFormat:
The first line of the input contains two integers N — the length of array A, and K.
The second line of the input contains N integers A1 , A2 , . . . , AN.
outputFormat: Print a single integer — the minimum number of elements to replace in A to satisfy the conditions for the challenge.

name: Subarray Permutation
description:
You are given an array A, permutation of integers from 1 to N, and you are required to solve a challenging problem.

You need to create a binary string, where Si is 1 if there is a subarray of A which is a permutation of integers from 1 to i, otherwise Si is 0.

An array C is a subarray of an array B if C can be obtained from B by deletion of several (possibly, zero or all) elements from the beginning and several (possibly, zero or all) elements from the end.
constraints:
1 ≤ N ≤ 2 × 105

1 ≤ Ai ≤ N

All Ai are distinct.
inputFormat:
The first line of the input contains a single integer N  — the length of array A.

The second line of the input contains N integers A1 , A2 , . . . , AN — the given permutation.
outputFormat: Print a binary string, i.e. consisting of only 0 and 1, the required output.

name: Not This Array
description:
Mehul has an array A consisting of N non-negative integers. He isn’t liking the array the way it is, so he decides to make a new array B.

The array B is formed by taking some elements from the starting end of A, and appending the MEX of those elements to B. Then those elements are erased, shifting the remaining elements of A.

The MEX of a set of non-negative integers is the minimum non-negative integer which isn’t in the set.
Mehul also wishes that the new array B is as big as possible, so he decides to make B lexicographically maximum.

An array x is lexicographically greater than an array y if in the first where x and y differ xi > yi or if sizeof(x)> sizeof(y) and y is a prefix of x.

Find out the array B that Mehul would have constructed.
inputFormat:
The first line of the input contains a single integer N  — the length of array A.

The second line of the input contains N integers A1 , A2 , . . . , AN.
outputFormat: Print the length M, of the lexicographically maximum array B, Mehul would create, followed by M integers denoting the elements of B, in a space-separated manner on the next line.

name: No Ones
description:
Monu Bhaiya has a binary string S of length N (a binary string is a string consisting of symbols 0 and 1). He isn’t a fan of positive integers these days so he doesn’t want any 1’s in his string.

However, to achieve this he won’t be simply changing them or removing them instead, he asks you for help. He only allows you to perform a special operation wherein, you pick a prefix of the string, flip the bits in it (i.e. change the 0 to 1 and 1 to 0), and reverse the prefix.

Now this would be a very simple tasks, so to spice it up, you have restrained yourself of getting rid of all 1’s in no more than N operations and no operation on a longer prefix can be applied before a shorter prefix, i.e. the operations must be in increasing order of prefix length and also no operation should be repeated.

Find out whether it is possible to achieve a 0-string (consisting of only 0’s), with the above constraints, if so output the lengths of prefixes in their order of operations.
constraints:
1 ≤ N ≤ 2 × 105

S only consists of symbols 0 and 1.
inputFormat:
The first line of the input contains a single integer N — the length of the binary string S.

The second line of the input contains a binary string, S of length N.
outputFormat: Print an integer K — the number of operations required, followed by K space – separated integers P1 , P2 , . . . , PK (1 ≤ Pi ≤ N), where Pi is the length of the prefix to be flipped and reversed. If it isn’t possible to do so, print -1.

name: Marathon Stat-keeper
description:
An official stat-keeper is a sports official who keeps track of various events during a game. This data is further used in future by the competitors to strategically advance themselves with respect to their games in addition to their game skills.
 Different games have different types of stats to keep track of.

Mohan is a Marathon Stat-keeper, his primary role requires him to keep track of the number of athletes who overtake any other athlete between any two instances of the marathon.

Since a very large number of athletes usually participate, tracking the overtakes for each and every athlete would take him a lot of time and work.
You are given two instances of the leader-board of the marathon, i.e. the order of athletes at times S and E (S surely overtook some of the other athletes in between these instances.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N, the number of athletes in the run.

The next line contains N space-separated integers, S1, S2,…., SN, denoting the bib numbers of the athletes in order of their rank on the leader-board at the first instance.

The next line also contains N space-separated integers, E1, E2,…., EN, denoting the bib numbers of the athletes in order of their rank on the leader-board at the second instance.

All the Siand Ei are unique and a permutation of first N integers.
outputFormat: Print a single integer — the number of athletes that surely overtook some other athlete in between these instances.

name: Char Transform
description:
Neetu has a word(string) consisting of all lowercase English letters. Her friend gives her another word and a list of words.

A Char Transformation from a beginWord to an endWord using a dictionary wordList is a sequence of words such that all the words in the sequence must belong to wordList except the beginWord, and any two adjacent words may differ in at most one character.

The first and last words of the sequence must be beginWord and endWord respectively.
Neetu wishes to find all the different Char Transformations from her word to the one given by her friend using the list. Help her report all the shortest Char Transformations possible.

Second line contains an integer N, denoting the number of words in wordlist.

Next line contains N, space-separated strings.

Print all the Char Transformations of the shortest length on a new-line with the words in the sequence separated by a space.

hit fog
6

hit hot lot log fog

Uttam just learn about palindrome. Adarsh gives him a task to find out total number of substrings that are palindrome of a given string s. Help Uttam to find out total number of palindromic substring.

 Note: A substring is a contiguous sequence of characters within the string.

Given an array of non-negative integers arr, A monkey is initially positioned at the first index of the array.Each element in the array arr[i] represents the maximum
length of a forward jump from index i .Monkey wants to reach the last index in the minimum number of jumps. Help Monkey to find that.

It is guaranteed that Monkey can always reach the last index.
inputFormat:
First line takes integer N(size of array) as input.

Second line contains N integers initializing to each index of the array respectively.
outputFormat: Print the min number of jumps Monkey needs to reach at the last index.

name: On a Mission With Pathan and Tiger
description: Pathan is on a mission with Tiger. They decide to send messages to each other using a sequence of N elements in random order. To decode the message they will arrange the elements in increasing order and remove the duplicates if any are present. Now you joined Pathan and Tiger in the mission and it's your task to decode the message and send only useful parts to them.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the size of Sequence N.
The second line contains the N elements of the Sequence in space separated manner.
outputFormat: Print the unique elements in increasing order

name: Unique number  of occurrences.
description: Given an array of integers , now you have to return true if and only if the number of occurrences of each value in the array is unique.
inputFormat:
First line of  input contains integer n, denoting the size of the array.
The next line contains n space separated integers denoting the elements of the array.
outputFormat: Print true if and only if the number of occurrences of each value in the array is unique, otherwise print false.

name: Non- Allergic Array
description:
You hate Repeated numbers. You want to remove all the duplicate elements in the array.

You are given an integer array sorted in **non-decreasing** order, remove the duplicates in-place such that each unique element appears only once. The relative order of the elements should be kept the same.
inputFormat:
First Line contains an Integer **N** (size of array).

Second Line contains an integer array.
outputFormat: Print the new Array

name: Two sum
description: You are given an array of integers nums and an integer target. Your task is to find two distinct indices i and j such that nums[i] + nums[j] == target. Return the indices as an array [i, j]. Assume there is exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.
inputFormat:
- An integer n (the number of elements in the array).
- An integer target.
- An array of integers nums of size n.
outputFormat: - An array [i, j] containing two indices of the array nums such that nums[i] + nums[j] == target. The indices i and j should satisfy i ≠ j. Indices are 0-based. If there are not such valid index with given target print -1 -1.

name: Special Subarray
description:
You are given an array of numbers. A subarray is considered special if it contains exactly k **odd** numbers. Your task is to find the number of special subarrays in the given array.

Given an array of integers nums and an integer k.
Return the number of **special sub-arrays**.
inputFormat:
First Line contains two space-separated integers **N** (size of the array)  and **k**.

Second Line contains an integer array.
outputFormat: Print total number of special subarrays.

name: Squares of sorted array
description:
You are very fond of finding squares of a number. You want to sort an integer array after finding squares of each number.

You are given an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order, print an array of the ***squares*** of each number **sorted** in non-decreasing order.
inputFormat:
First Line contains an integer **N** (size of the array) .

Second Line contains an integer array.
outputFormat: Print squared-sorted array.

name: Yet Another Game problem
description:
Monu and Rajesh Bhaiya with their friend Mr Block engaged in a fascinating game involving N items, each item containing a distinct number. The game was simple yet strategically engaging: Monu and Rajesh, the players, took turns selecting an item from either the leftmost or rightmost position in the row.

Their objective was to maximize their individual sums of selected item numbers. The players take turns, and Rajesh moves first. During his turn a player can take one item : either the leftmost item in a row or the rightmost one. The game ends when there is no more items .

Rajesh and Monu Bhaiya are being greedy. Each of them chooses the item with the larger number during his move.

Mr Block  knows which strategy the guys are using, so he wants to determine the final score, given the initial state of the game.
inputFormat:
First Line contains an integer **N** i.e. size of the array.

Second line contains an integer array .
outputFormat: Print their scores. The first number is the number of Rajesh points at the end of the game, the second number is the number of Monu points at the end.

name: Broken Keys
description:
Recently Priya noticed that some of the buttons of his keyboard are malfunctioning. For simplicity, we assume that Priya's keyboard contains 26
 buttons (one for each letter of the Latin alphabet). Each button is either working fine or malfunctioning.

To check which buttons need replacement, Priya pressed some buttons in sequence, and a string s
 appeared on the screen. When Priya presses a button with character c
, one of the following events happened:

if the button was working correctly, a character c
 appeared at the end of the string Priya was typing;
if the button was malfunctioning, two characters c
 appeared at the end of the string.
For example, suppose the buttons corresponding to characters a and c are working correctly, and the button corresponding to b is malfunctioning. If Priya presses the buttons in the order a, b, a, c, a, b, a, then the string he is typing changes as follows: a →
 abb →
 abba →
 abbac →
 abbaca →
 abbacabb →
 abbacabba.

You are given a string s
 which appeared on the screen after Priya pressed some buttons. Help Priya to determine which buttons are working correctly for sure (that is, this string could not appear on the screen if any of these buttons was malfunctioning).

You may assume that the buttons don't start malfunctioning when Priya types the string: each button either works correctly throughout the whole process, or malfunctions throughout the whole process.

***Note :  The string res
 should contain all characters which correspond to buttons that work correctly in alphabetical order, without any separators or repetitions***
inputFormat: Single line consisting of a string of lowercase letters.
outputFormat: print one line containing a string res.

name: Linear Keyboard
description:
You are given a keyboard that consists of 26
 keys. The keys are arranged sequentially in one row in a certain order. Each key corresponds to a **unique lowercase** Latin letter.

You have to type the word ***s***
 on this keyboard. It also consists only of lowercase Latin letters.

To type a word, you need to type all its letters consecutively one by one. To type each letter you must position your hand exactly over the corresponding key and press it.

Moving the hand between the keys takes time which is equal to the **absolute value** of the difference between positions of these keys (the keys are numbered from left to right). No time is spent on pressing the keys and on placing your hand over the first letter of the word.

For example, consider a keyboard where the letters from 'a' to 'z' are arranged in consecutive alphabetical order. The letters 'h', 'e', 'l' and 'o' then are on the positions 8
, 5
, 12
 and 15
, respectively. Therefore, it will take |5−8|+|12−5|+|12−12|+|15−12|=13
 units of time to type the word "hello".

Determine how long it will take to print the word s
.
inputFormat:
The first line of a description contains a keyboard — a string of length 26

 which consists only of lowercase Latin letters. Each of the letters from 'a' to 'z' appears exactly once on the keyboard.

The second line of the input contains the word s.
outputFormat: Print  the **minimal time** it takes to type the word s on the given keyboard.

name: 3 sum
description:
Your Lucky number is 3 . You wants to find out whether there exist a triplet whose sum ends in the digit 3.

More Formally ,

You are given an array a of positive integers with length **n**, determine if there exist three distinct indices i, j, k such that `a`i+`a`j+`a`k ends in the digit 3.

Print "**YES**" if triplets exist otherwise print "**NO**"
inputFormat:
First Line contains an integer N .

Second line contains an integer array A of size N .
outputFormat: Print "YES" or "NO" accordingly.

name: Selfless Product of Array
description:
You are given an integer array nums and
**Selfless Product** of an element `nums[i]`  can be defined as product of all elements of the array except itself.

Print an array answer such that answer[i] is equal to the product of all the elements of nums except nums[i].

***Note:  The product of any prefix or suffix of nums is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit integer***.
inputFormat:
First Line contains an integer N (size of the array) .

Second Line contains an array.
outputFormat: Print an array of selfless products.

name: Alice's Array Adventure
description:
In the realm of Coding Blocks, Alice, a lover of odd numbers, embarked on a quest to find the sum of all odd-length subarrays of a given array. Seeking aid, she turned to Mr. Block, renowned for his problem-solving skills.

Given an array arr[] consisting of N integers, the task is to find the sum of all the elements of all possible subarrays of odd length.
inputFormat:
First Line contains an integer N (size of the array) .

Second Line contains an array.
outputFormat: Print the sum of all possible odd-length subarrays of arr.

name: Arrange Coins
description:
Rajesh Bhaiya is playing a game with coins. He has **N** coins in total.

Rajesh Bhaiya wants to build a staircase with these coins. The staircase consists of k rows where the `ith` row has exactly `i` coins. The last row of the staircase may be incomplete.

 Print the number of complete rows of the staircase Rajesh Bhaiya will build.
Note : Expected TC is O(log n).
inputFormat: Single Line consisting of a total number of coins represented by **N**
outputFormat: Print the number of complete rows of the staircase .

name: Monotonous array
description:
In the land of Coding Blocks, Ram was fascinated by the concept of monotonic arrays, those that either consistently increase or decrease. Eager to explore this, he set out to determine if a given array followed this pattern.

With an array of integers, nums, in hand, Mr. Block embarked on the analysis. He meticulously compared each pair of elements, checking if they adhered to either an increasing or decreasing trend throughout the array. His keen observation skills allowed him to determine if the array was truly monotonic, satisfying Ram's curiosity.
inputFormat:
First Line contains an integer N (size of the array) .

Second Line contains an array.
outputFormat: Print "True" or "False".

name: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array
description:
Ram wants to find out all the missing number from `1` to `n`  in the array **nums**. He needs your help in this problem.

You are given an array `nums` of `n` integers where `nums[i]` is in the range `[1, n]` , Print a **sorted** array of all the integers in the range `[1, n]` that do not appear in nums.
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N.

Second line contains an integer array of size N.
outputFormat: Print sorted array of all the missing numbers.

name: Non-Decreasing Array
description:
Kartik loves sorted array . He wants to make array sorted by performing exactly one operation. He needs your help for this problem.

You are given an array ***nums*** with `n` integers, your task is to check if it could become **non-decreasing** by modifying at most one element.

We define an array is non-decreasing if a[i] <= a[i + 1] holds for every i (0-based) such that (0 <= i <= n - 2).

Print "**YES**" if you can transform the array in its sorted form other wise "**NO**".
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N.

Second line contains an integer array of size N.
outputFormat: Print "YES" or "NO" accordingly.

name: String Split
description:
Balanced strings are those that have an equal quantity of 'L' and 'R' characters.

Given a balanced string s, split it into some number of substrings such that:

Each substring is balanced.
Return the maximum number of balanced strings you can obtain.
inputFormat: string is given as input
outputFormat: output the maximum balanced strings

name: Three closest elements from the given three sorted arrays
description:
You are given three sorted arrays A[], B[] and C[], find 3 elements i, j and k from A, B and C respectively such that :

max ( abs (A[i] – B[j]), abs ( B[j] – C[k]), abs ( C[k] – A[i] )) is **minimized**.

 Here abs() indicates **absolute**  value.
inputFormat:
First Line contains  p, q and r i.e size of the Array A , B and C respectively.

Next three Lines contain arrays A , B and C respectively.
outputFormat: Print a number from each array such that the given condition is satisfied.

name: string reversal
description: Varu loves coding and want his freind to improve as well so he has given  task to his freind to reverse the string.
inputFormat: First Line is given as a string input
outputFormat: output the reversed string

name: Rahul Loves Strings
description: Rahul has  two strings S and T. He will be happy only if any substring of string T contains a permutation of string S, your task is to tell whether rahul is happy or not. If he is happy print "YES" else print "NO".
inputFormat: String S and T will be given as Input
outputFormat: Print YES or NO (Case Sensitive)

name: Compress string
description:
Given a string compress it using the following algorithm:

Begin with an empty string s. For each group of consecutive repeating characters in string:

If the group's length is 1, append the character to s.
Otherwise, append the character followed by the group's length.
The compressed string s should not be returned separately, but instead, be stored in the input character array chars. Note that group lengths that are 10 or longer will be split into multiple characters in chars.

After you are done modifying the input array, return the new length of the array.

You must write an algorithm that uses only constant extra space.
inputFormat: String input is given
outputFormat: the new length of the array.

name: Generous Kefa
description: One day Kefa found n baloons. For convenience, we denote color of i-th baloon as s[i] — lowercase letter of the Latin alphabet. Also Kefa has k friends. Friend will be upset, If he get two baloons of the same color. Kefa want to give out all baloons to his friends. Help Kefa to find out, can he give out all his baloons, such that no one of his friens will be upset — print «YES», if he can, and «NO», otherwise. Note, that Kefa's friend will not upset, if he doesn't get baloons at all.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers n and k .
Next line contains string s
outputFormat: Answer to the task —YES or NO in a single line.

name: String multiplication
description: Given two non-negative integers num1 and num2 represented as strings, return the product of num1 and num2, also represented as a string.
inputFormat: first line contains space seperated strings
outputFormat: return product

name: Consecutive Ones
description: You are given a binary array (an array consisting of only 0s and 1s). Your task is to find the maximum number of consecutive 1s in the array.
constraints:
- 1 ≤ n ≤ 105
- Each element of the array is either 0 or 1.
inputFormat:
- The first line contains an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 105), the size of the array.
- The second line contains n space-separated integers, where each integer is either 0 or 1.
outputFormat: Print a single integer, representing the maximum number of consecutive 1s in the given binary array.

name: DNA Sequences
description:
The DNA sequence is composed of a series of nucleotides abbreviated as 'A', 'C', 'G', and 'T'.

For example, "ACGAATTCCG" is a DNA sequence.
When studying DNA, it is useful to identify repeated sequences within the DNA.

Given a string s that represents a DNA sequence, return all the 10-letter-long sequences (substrings) that occur more than once in a DNA molecule. You may return the answer in lexographical order.
inputFormat: a string s that represents a DNA sequence,
outputFormat: return all the 10-letter-long sequences (substrings) that occur more than once in a DNA molecule

name: Tight Triplets
description:
A tight triplet is defined as a triplet of integers, where the maximum and the minimum differ by no more than 2.

For a triplet {a, b, c}, max(a, b, c) – min(a, b, c) ≤ 2.

You are given an array A of size N, consisting of integers from 1 to N, find out the number of possible tight triplets.
inputFormat:
The first line of the input contains an integer N.

The second line of the input contains N space-separated integers, A1, A2, . . . , AN.
outputFormat: Print a single integer - the number of tight triplets possible from the given array.

name: Reverse Vowels
description:
You are given a string 's'. Reverse only the vowels in the string and then return it.

The vowels are 'a', 'e', 'i', 'o', and 'u', and they can appear in both uppercase and lowercase.
constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 3 * 10^5

s consist of printable ASCII characters.
inputFormat: A string 's'.
outputFormat: A string with reversed vowels.

name: Missing Ranges
description: Given a sorted integer array nums, where the range of elements are in the inclusive range [lower, upper], print its missing ranges.
inputFormat:
First line contains 3-space separated Integers N (size of array) , Lower and Upper values .

Second Line consists of an array nums.
outputFormat: Print each Missing Range in a new Line.

name: Valid Word
description:
Given a string s, determine if it is valid.

A string s is valid if, starting with an empty string t = "", you can transform t into s after performing the following operation any number of times:

Insert string "abc" into any position in t. More formally, t becomes tleft + "abc" + tright, where t == tleft + tright. Note that tleft and tright  may be empty.
inputFormat: String
outputFormat: Print true if s is a valid string, otherwise, Print false.

name: Partition this string
description:
You are given a string s. We want to partition the string into as many parts as possible so that each letter appears in at most one part.

Note that the partition is done so that after concatenating all the parts in order, the resultant string should be s.

Output the number of characters in each partition, separated by space.
constraints:
1 <= s.length() <= 500

s consists of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: A string.
outputFormat: Space-separated integers, representing the sizes of each partition.

name: The Number K
description:
Rohan has given a number **N**. He wants to minimize the given number with his magic stick of power **K**.

Magic stick of power **K** can delete exactly **K** digits from the number .
He needed your help in this problem.

 You are given a string num representing a non-negative integer ***num***, and an integer ***k***, Print the smallest possible integer after removing k digits from num.
constraints:
1 5

num consists of only digits.

num does not have any leading zeros except for the zero itself.
inputFormat:
First line contains a string num representing a non-negative integer.

Second line contains an integer K.
outputFormat: Print the smallest possible integer.

name: Beautiful String
description:
A string s is said to be  Beautiful String  if s can be palindrome after deleting at most one character from it.

Given a string s , Print True if s is a beautiful string .
inputFormat: Single line consists of a string  s
outputFormat: Print "True" or "False"

name: Subsets
description:
Given an integer array arr of unique elements, return all possible subsets (the power set).

The solution set must not contain duplicate subsets.Print the solution in sorted order.

Note: Please watch the output format once before submitting.
constraints:
1 <= N <= 10

-100 <= arr[i] <= 100

All arr[i] must be unique element.
inputFormat:
First line takes an integer N(size of array)
Second Line contains N space separated integers describing array
outputFormat: Print all possible subsets, Each subset is in new line and all subsets must be in sorted order.

name: Magic Swap Number
description:
You are given an integer N. You can swap two digits at most once to get the maximum valued number and the swap is called as  Magic Swap

Print the value of N after performing Magic Swap operation on N .
inputFormat: A positive integer number
outputFormat: Print N after performing Magic Swap

name: Sentence screen fitting
description:
Given a rows x cols screen and a sentence represented as a list of strings, print the number of times the given sentence can be fitted on the screen.

The order of words in the sentence must remain unchanged, and a word cannot be split into two lines. A single space must separate two consecutive words in a line.
inputFormat:
First Line contains three space-separated Integers N(number of words in sentence ) , Rows and Cols .

Second Line contains an array of strings (sentence)
outputFormat: Print the desired output .

name: Merge Two Sorted Linked Lists
description:
You are given the heads of two sorted linked lists l1 and l2.

Merge the two lists in a one sorted list. The list should be made by splicing together the nodes of the first two lists.

 Your task is to print the merged linked list.
constraints:
The number of nodes in both lists is in the range [0, 100].

-100 non-decreasing order.
inputFormat:
First line contains two space separated integers specifying the size of both the list.

Second line contains the elements of first list.

Third line contains the elements of second list.
outputFormat:
Print the merged linked list.

*If there is no element in the merged linked list then print -1*

name: Partition the List
description:
There is a group of friends which walks together and they are connected to eack other like a linked list .
With each friend there is some power associated.
while walking there may come barrier in which there every friend  needs at least that much power to overcome that so after that barrier the friend will be partioned in a way such that the friends with less power then that to overcome that barrier will come before the friends who can easily overcome that.
constraints:
The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 200].

-100 <= Node.val <= 100

-200 <= x <= 200
inputFormat:
First line contains the number of friends-N
Second line contains the power associated with N friends.
Third line contains the barrier value.
outputFormat: Print the list after partitioning it.

name: Remove Kth Node From End of List
description:
You are given the head of a singly linked list and an integer k. Your task is to remove the k-th node
        from the end of the list and return the head of the modified list.
inputFormat:
- The first line contains an integer n — the size of the linked list.
- The second line contains n space-separated integers, representing the elements of the linked list.
- The third line contains an integer k, the position of the node to remove from the end.
outputFormat:
Output a single line containing the elements of the modified linked list, separated by spaces.
Note: Do not modify or change anything inside the main function.

name: LRU Cache
description:
Design and Implement methods of LRU Cache .
It has 2 methods, get()  and set()  which are defined as follows.

get(x)   :  Returns the value of the key x if the key exists in the cache otherwise returns -1.

set(x,y) :  Update the value of the key if the key exists. Otherwise, add the key-value pair to the cache. If the number of keys exceeds the capacity from this operation, evict the least recently used key.

In the constructor of the class the size of the cache should be intitialized.
inputFormat:
The first line of input contain an integer T denoting the number of test cases. Then T test case follow. Each test case contains 3 lines. The first line of input contains an integer N denoting the capacity of the cache and then in the next line is an integer Q denoting the number of queries Then Q queries follow. A Query can be of two types
1. SET x y : sets the value of the key x with value y
2. GET x : gets the key of x if present else returns -1.
outputFormat: For each test case, in a new line, output will be space separated values of the query.
sampleInput:
2
2
2
SET 1 2 GET 1
2
7
SET 1 2 SET 2 3 SET 1 5 SET 4 5 SET 6 7 GET 4 GET 1

name: Merge K sorted linked lists
description: Given K sorted linked lists of different sizes. The task is to merge them in such a way that after merging they will be a single sorted linked list.
inputFormat: First line of input contains number of testcases T. For each testcase, first line of input contains number of linked lists N and next line contains data of nodes of all K linked lists, with first element as M, the length of linked list and next M elements for the same linked list.
outputFormat: For each testcase, in a new line, print the merged linked list.

name: Perform Removal Operation on Sorted List
description: Given the head of a sorted linked list, delete all nodes that have duplicate numbers, leaving only distinct numbers from the original list. Return the linked list sorted as well.
constraints:
The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 300].

-100 <= Node.val <= 100

The list is guaranteed to be sorted in ascending order.
inputFormat:
Int n size of the linked list

n elements which are the value of the n nodes
outputFormat:
Print the updated linked list

If there is no such element in the updated linked list then print -1 as a delimitation.

name: Lab Evaluation
description: Shivam is having his Data Structure and Algorithms lab evaluation. His teacher gave him a list which has sequential access. Now, Shivam has to sort this given list in ascending order.
constraints:
The size of list is in the range [0, 5 * 104].

-105 5
inputFormat:
First line contains n, size of list

Second line contains n numbers which are the values
outputFormat: Print the sorted list

name: Three Sum Closest
description:
Monu Bhaiya brings N no. of balls with each ball having some number printed. Monu bhaiya gives task to his students to find closest number to a target by adding of any three balls . You are his one of the brilliant student so find that closest number and prove your brilliance again.

You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution.
inputFormat:
First line takes two integers N(no. of balls) and target number.

Second line contains N integers a1,a2,a3,...an describing number printed on each ball
outputFormat: Print the closest sum of any three balls to target value.

name: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
description: Given a sorted array and you just need to remove the duplicates from the array
constraints:
Length of the array is less than 150000

The array is in ascending order
inputFormat:
First line contains integer N as size of array.

Next line contains a N integer as element of array.
outputFormat:
The first line prints the new reduced length
The second line prints the elements of the array till the new length

name: Monotonic Array
description:
Given an array nums. Check whether it is monotonic in nature.
An array can be monotonic increasing or monotonic decreasing.
An array nums is monotone increasing if for all i = nums[j].

Your task is to return true if the given array is monotonic, or false otherwise.
inputFormat:
The first line contains N, the size of the array.

The second line contains N space-separated integers.
outputFormat: Print the string "true" or "false" as per the given conditions.

name: Array partition
description:
You are given an integer array nums of **2*n** integers, group these integers into n pairs (a1, b1), (a2, b2), ..., (an, bn) such that the sum of min(ai, bi) for all i is maximized.

Print the **maximized sum**.
inputFormat:
First Line contains an integer N.

Second Line contains an integer array.
outputFormat: Print the maximized sum

name: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
description:
You are given a sorted array of unique integers that has been rotated at some pivot unknown to you beforehand. You are also given a target value. Your task is to find the index of the target in this rotated array.
If the target does not exist, return -1.
constraints:
- 1 ≤ n ≤ 105
- -109 ≤ array[i], target ≤ 109
- All integers in the array are unique.
inputFormat:
- The first line contains an integer n — the size of the array.
- The second line contains n space-separated integers, representing the rotated sorted array.
- The third line contains an integer target — the value to search for.
outputFormat: Output a single integer — the index of the target in the array. If the target is not found, return -1.

name: Circular subarray maximum
description:
Given a circular integer array nums of length n, return the maximum possible sum of a non-empty subarray of nums.

A circular array means the end of the array connects to the beginning of the array. Formally, the next element of nums[i] is nums[(i + 1) % n] and the previous element of nums[i] is nums[(i - 1 + n) % n].

A subarray may only include each element of the fixed buffer nums at most once. Formally, for a subarray nums[i], nums[i + 1], ..., nums[j], there does not exist i <= k1, k2 <= j with k1 % n == k2 % n.
inputFormat:
First Line contain Size of array
Second Line has array elements
outputFormat: return maximum sum

name: Patching Array
description:
Given a sorted integer array nums and an integer n, add/patch elements to the array such that any number in the range [1, n] inclusive can be formed by the sum of some elements in the array.

Return the minimum number of patches required.
constraints:
1 4

nums is sorted in ascending order.
1 <= n <= 2^31 - 1
inputFormat: You are given with N array elements and k.
outputFormat: Return the minimum number of patches required.

name: Cheems and the Valentine’s Day Magic Stick 💖✨
description:
It was Valentine’s Day in DoggoLand 🐶, and Cheems was on a special mission! 💌 He wanted to create the longest chain of love 💕, but there was a problem—his Love Chain 💞 (a binary array of size N) had some gaps (0's) 😢, breaking the streak of pure love (1's) ❤️.

But fear not! Cheems had a Magic Stick 🪄, gifted by the Love Fairy 🧚‍♀️. This stick had K magical powers, allowing him to flip at most K broken links (0’s) into true love (1’s) ❤️.

Now, Cheems needed to maximize the longest streak of consecutive love (1’s) 💘 by using his magic wisely 🎩✨. His goal? To make the longest, unbreakable chain of love 💞 so that no heart ever felt lonely again!

name: Next Greater permutation
description:
The **Next greater  permutation** of an array of integers is the next ***lexicographically*** greater permutation of its integer.

More formally, if all the permutations of the array are sorted in one container according to their lexicographical order, then the next permutation of that array is the permutation that follows it in the sorted container. If such arrangement is not possible, the array must be rearranged as the lowest possible order (i.e., sorted in ascending order).

You are given an Array **A** of size **N** consisting positive numbers  . Find the next greater permutation of Array A.
inputFormat:

name: Mr Block and Bear

Mr. Block has a string s = s1s2... s|s| (where |s| denotes the string's length), consisting of lowercase English letters. Mr. Block wants to count the number of pairs of indices i, j (1 ≤ i ≤ j ≤ |s|) such that the string x(i, j) = sisi+1... sj contains at least one occurrence of the word "bear" as a substring.

name: Mr Blocks and land of Algorithmia

.

.

name: Books
description:
When Valera has got some free time, he goes to the library to read some books. Today he's got **t** free minutes to read. That's why Valera took **n** books in the library and for each book he estimated the time he is going to need to read it. Let's number the books by integers from `1` to `n`. Valera needs ai minutes to read the i-th book.

Valera decided to choose an arbitrary book with number `i` and read the books one by one, starting from this book. In other words, he will first read book number i, then book number i + 1, then book number i + 2 and so on. He continues the process until he either runs out of the free time or finishes reading the n-th book. Valera reads each book up to the end, that is, he doesn't start reading the book if he doesn't have enough free time to finish reading it.

Print the maximum number of books Valera can read.

name: Mr Block and Games
description:
Mr Block is organizing a football tournament. He has come up with the following tournament format:

- In the first several (possibly zero) stages, while the number of teams is even, they split in pairs and play one game for each pair. At each stage, the loser of each pair is eliminated (there are no draws). Such stages are held while the number of teams is even.
-  Eventually, there will be an odd number of teams remaining. If there is one team remaining, it will be declared the winner, and the tournament ends. Otherwise each of the remaining teams will play with each other remaining team once in round robin tournament (if there are x teams, there will be ![link](https://espresso.codeforces.com/633d3cd6417e5c6e9ea549a0e8c5ec3fedb38b92.png) games), and the tournament ends.

For example, if there were 20 teams initially, they would begin by playing 10 games. So, 10 teams would be eliminated, and the remaining 10 would play 5 games. Then the remaining 5 teams would play 10 games in a round robin tournament. In total there would be 10+5+10=25 games.

Mr Block has already booked the stadium for n games. Help him to determine how many teams he should invite so that the tournament needs exactly n games. You should print all possible numbers of teams that will yield exactly n games in ascending order, or -1 if there are no such numbers.
inputFormat: The first line contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^18), the number of games that should be played.
outputFormat: Print all possible numbers of invited teams in ascending order, one per line. If exactly n games cannot be played, output one number: -1.

He listens to song number `i` **c** times. Rohan's play list is organized as follows: first song number 1 plays c1 times, then song number 2 plays c2 times, ....., in the end the song number n plays cn times.

Mayank took a piece of paper and wrote out **m** moments of time when he liked a song. Now for each such moment he wants to know the number of the song that played at that moment. The moment ***x*** means that Rohan wants to know which song was playing during the ***x-th*** minute of his listening to the play list.

It is guaranteed that there isn't such moment of time vi, when the music doesn't play any longer. It is guaranteed that vi 5 means that Mayank wants to know which song was playing during the vi-th minute from the start of listening to the playlist.

name: Day at the Beach
description:
One day Squidward, Spongebob and Patrick decided to go to the beach. Unfortunately, the weather was bad, so the friends were unable to ride waves. However, they decided to spent their time building sand castles.

At the end of the day there were n castles built by friends. Castles are numbered from 1 to n, and the height of the i-th castle is equal to hi. When friends were about to leave, Squidward noticed, that castles are not ordered by their height, and this looks ugly. Now friends are going to reorder the castles in a way to obtain that condition hi ≤ hi + 1 holds for all i from 1 to n - 1.

Squidward suggested the following process of sorting castles:

Castles are split into blocks — groups of consecutive castles. Therefore the block from i to j will include castles i, i + 1, ..., j. A block may consist of a single castle.
The partitioning is chosen in such a way that every castle is a part of exactly one block.
Each block is sorted independently from other blocks, that is the sequence hi, hi + 1, ..., hj becomes sorted.
The partitioning should satisfy the condition that after each block is sorted, the sequence hi becomes sorted too. This may always be achieved by saying that the whole sequence is a single block.
Even Patrick understands that increasing the number of blocks in partitioning will ease the sorting process. Now friends ask you to count the maximum possible number of blocks in a partitioning that satisfies all the above requirements.
inputFormat:
The first line of the input contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100 000) — the number of castles Spongebob, Patrick and Squidward made from sand during the day.

The next line contains n integers hi (1 ≤ hi ≤ 109). The i-th of these integers corresponds to the height of the i-th castle.
outputFormat: Print the maximum possible number of blocks in a valid partitioning

name: Mr Block is Perfect Normal Form
description:
Mr. Block lived in a world where strings were the building blocks of communication, each consisting of lowercase English letters. In this world, strings "s" and "t" were considered **isomorphic** if they had the same length and for every pair of positions "i" and "j," either "s[i] = s[j] and t[i] = t[j]" or "s[i] ≠ s[j] and t[i] ≠ t[j]." For instance, "abcac" and "zyxzx" were isomorphic, while "abcac" and "ppppp" were not.

A string "s" was said to be in **Normal form** if, for every string "t" that was **isomorphic** to "s," "s" was less than or equal to "t" when compared lexicographically. For example, "abcac" was in normal form because it was less than or equal to any string isomorphic to it, like "zyxzx."

One day, a puzzling challenge arose in Mr. Block's world. Given an integer "N," the task was to print all strings of length "N" that were in normal form, in lexicographically ascending order. This challenge intrigued Mr. Block, as it required a deep understanding of isomorphic relationships between strings and the ability to arrange them correctly.

Determined to solve the puzzle, Mr. Block embarked on a journey through the world of strings, carefully analyzing their structures and relationships. With perseverance and clever thinking, Mr. Block finally cracked the code, uncovering the secrets of these isomorphic and normal strings. His solution revealed the hidden patterns and order within the world of strings, showcasing his exceptional problem-solving skills and determination.
inputFormat: First line contains N.
outputFormat: Print all strings of length N that are in normal form.

void addAtTail(int val) Append a node of value val as the last element of the linked list.

void addAtIndex(int index, int val) Add a node of value val before the indexth node in the linked list. If index equals the length of the linked list, the node will be appended to the end of the linked list. If index is greater than the length, the node will not be inserted.

void deleteAtIndex(int index) Delete the indexth node in the linked list, if the index is valid.

name: Password Cracker
description:
In the small town of Codeville, there was a renowned institution known as Coding Blocks Academy, famous for solving complex coding puzzles. One day, the Academy received a peculiar challenge from Mr. Blocks, a legendary coder known for his cryptic tasks.

The challenge involved a mysterious encoded string named 'Stringy'. The task was to decode Stringy using a special method: If a character was a letter, it would be noted down and printed as it is. If it was a digit, the entire decoded sequence so far had to be repeated that many times minus one (If the character read is a digit d, the entire current tape is repeatedly written d - 1 more times in total).

The brightest student at the Academy, young Ellie, accepted the challenge. She carefully read Stringy, applying the rules with precision. The decoded message grew, a beautiful pattern of repetition and sequence.

Her final task was to find the kth letter in the decoded string. Ellie, with her sharp skills, quickly identified the letter. Mr. Blocks, impressed by her talent and the Academy's teaching, revealed that the letter was a clue to his next coding puzzle.

The students of Coding Blocks Academy celebrated, proud of unraveling yet another of Mr. Blocks' coding challenges, and eager for the next.

2 9

It is guaranteed that k is less than or equal to the length of the decoded string.

The decoded string is guaranteed to have less than 263 letters.

name: Ball Collision

We are given an array ball of integers representing balls in a row. Each ball contains a bomb inside them. Whenever two balls collide, they explode.

For each ball, the absolute value represents its size, and the sign represents its direction (positive meaning right, negative meaning left). Each ball moves at the same speed.

Find out the state of the balls after all collisions. If two balls meet, the smaller one will explode. If both are the same size, both will explode. Two balls moving in the same direction will never meet.

name: Final Interview Round
description:
Vamica is appearing in her final interview round of a company. Her interviewer after her introduction gave her a question on strings. Now, if she solves it correctly she will get selected. The question is as follows: She is given a string path, which is an absolute path (starting with a slash '/') to a file or directory in a Unix-style file system, she now has to convert it to the simplified canonical path.

In a Unix-style file system, a period '.' refers to the current directory, a double period '..' refers to the directory up a level, and any multiple consecutive slashes (i.e. '//') are treated as a single slash '/'. For this problem, any other format of periods such as '...' are treated as file/directory names.

The canonical path should have the following format:

1. The path starts with a single slash '/'.
2. Any two directories are separated by a single slash '/'.
3. The path does not end with a trailing '/'.
4. The path only contains the directories on the path from the root directory to the target file or directory (i.e., no period '.' or double period '..')

 3. Every close bracket has a corresponding open bracket of the same type.

name: Monu bhaiya and Baseball
description:
You are keeping score for a baseball game with strange rules. The game consists of several rounds, where the scores of past rounds may affect future rounds' scores.

At the beginning of the game, you start with an empty record. You are given a list of strings ops, where ops[i] is the ith operation you must apply to the record and is one of the following:

1. An integer x - Record a new score of x.
2. "+" - Record a new score that is the sum of the previous two scores. It is guaranteed there will always be two previous scores.
3. "D" - Record a new score that is double the previous score. It is guaranteed there will always be a previous score.
4. "C" - Invalidate the previous score, removing it from the record. It is guaranteed there will always be a previous score.

Return the sum of all the scores on the record.

Coding Blocks conducted a coding test for students to grab scholarships. The question was to find the next greater element of some element x in an array is the first greater element that is to the right of x in the same array.

For each 0 <= i < arr1.length, find the index j such that arr1[i] == arr2[j] and determine the next greater element of arr2[j] in arr2. If there is no next greater element, then the answer for this query is -1.

Nobita is having his chemistry assessment today. In his assessment his teacher gave a string of chemical formula. He now has to return count of each atom. However today he cannot take help from Doraemon because he has gone out on a Date with Mii-Chan. So, today you have to help Nobita in his assessment so that he doesn't score zero.

One or more digits representing that element's count may follow if the count is greater than 1. If the count is 1, no digits will follow.

For example, "H2O" and "H2O2" are possible, but "H1O2" is impossible.
Two formulas are concatenated together to produce another formula.

For example, "H2O2He3Mg4" is also a formula.
A formula placed in parentheses, and a count (optionally added) is also a formula.

For example, "(H2O2)" and "(H2O2)3" are formulas.
Print the count of all elements as a string in the following form: the first name (in sorted order), followed by its count (if that count is more than 1), followed by the second name (in sorted order), followed by its count (if that count is more than 1), and so on.

The test cases are generated so that all the values in the output fit in a 32-bit integer.

string is always valid.

name: Coloring the Composite
description:
A positive integer is called composite if it can be represented as a product of two positive integers, both greater than 1. For example, the following numbers are composite: 6, 4, 120, 27. The following numbers aren't: 1, 2, 3, 17, 97.

Alice is given a sequence of n composite numbers a1,a2,…,an.

She wants to choose an integer m≤11 and color each element one of m colors from 1 to m so that:

for each color from 1 to m there is at least one element of this color;
each element is colored and colored exactly one color;
the greatest common divisor of any two elements that are colored the same color is greater than 1, i.e. gcd(ai,aj)>1 for each pair i,j if these elements are colored the same color.
Note that equal elements can be colored different colors — you just have to choose one of m colors for each of the indices from 1 to n.

Alice showed already that if all ai≤1000 then she can always solve the task by choosing some m≤11.

Help Alice to find the required coloring. Note that you don't have to minimize or maximize the number of colors, you just have to find the solution with some m from 1 to 11.
inputFormat:
The first line of the test case contains a single integer n
The second line of the test case contains n composite integers a1,a2,…,an .
outputFormat:
For each test case print 2 lines. The first line should contain a single integer m (1≤m≤11) — the number of used colors. Consider colors to be numbered from 1 to m. The second line should contain any coloring that satisfies the above conditions. Print n integers c1,c2,…,cn (1≤c[i]≤m), where ci is the color of the i-th element. Note that you don't have to minimize or maximize the number of colors, you just have to find the solution with some m from 1 to 11.

Remember that each color from 1 to m should be used at least once. Any two elements of the same color should not be coprime (i.e. their GCD should be greater than 1).

name: Mr Blocks and His Soldiers
description:
In a land where soldiers played strategic games, two soldiers engaged in a unique challenge. The game began with the first soldier selecting a positive integer 'n' and passing it to the second soldier. The second soldier's goal was to maximize the number of rounds in the game.

Each round of the game involved the second soldier choosing a positive integer 'x' greater than 1, such that 'n' was divisible by 'x', and then replacing 'n' with 'n/x'. The game continued until 'n' became equal to 1, and there were no more valid moves left. At this point, the game ended, and the second soldier's score was equal to the number of rounds he had completed.

To add an intriguing twist to the game, the first soldier chose 'n' in the form of a factorial division, where 'n' was of the form 'a! / b!' for some positive integers 'a' and 'b', where 'a' was greater than or equal to 'b'. Here, 'k!' represented the factorial of 'k', which is the product of all positive integers not greater than 'k'.

The challenge for the second soldier was to devise a strategy to maximize his score given the initial value of 'n' in factorial form. The task required careful planning and calculation to determine the optimal values of 'x' to divide 'n' in each round. Can you figure out the maximum possible score the second soldier can achieve in this strategic game?

Then follow t lines, each contains pair of integers a and b (1 ≤ b ≤ a ≤ 5 000 000) defining the value of n for a game

A statement in Bit++ consists of only one operation and the variable "x", written without spaces. Executing a statement means performing the operation it contains. A program in Bit++ is a sequence of statements that need to be executed one after the other. The execution of a program means executing all the statements it contains, starting from an initial value of "x" equal to 0. The operation and variable can appear in any order within the statement, and there are no empty statements.

name: Bear and Prime Numbers

Recently, the bear started studying data structures and faced the following problem.

You are given a sequence of integers x1, x2, ..., xn of length n and m queries, each of them is characterized by two integers li, ri. Let's introduce f(p) to represent the number of such indexes k, that x[k] is divisible by p. The answer to the query li, ri is the sum: ,
  sigma(f(p)) , where p belongs to S(l[i],r[i])

 where S(l[i], r[i]) is a set of prime numbers from segment [li, ri] (both borders are included in the segment).

Help the bear cope with the problem.

 The second line contains n integers x1, x2, ..., xn .

Each of the following m lines contains a pair of space-separated integers, li and ri  — the numbers that characterize the current query.

In the land of Mr Block, there was a young mathematician named Alice. Alice loved numbers and puzzles more than anything else. One day, the town faced a problem: the Evil Count Divisor was casting a spell that made all numbers divisible by him disappear!

Determined to save her town, Alice set out on a quest. She knew that to break the spell, she needed to find all the prime numbers less than a given number, N.
