name: Kingdom Festival and Non-Coprime Numbers
description:
Once upon a time, there was a kingdom ruled by a wise and just king. The kingdom was home to many different tribes, each with their own unique customs and traditions. The king wanted to promote unity and harmony among the tribes, so he decided to host a grand festival where everyone could come together and celebrate.

To prepare for the festival, the king ordered his advisors to gather supplies and resources from all over the kingdom. Among the resources were bags of stones, each containing a different number of stones.

The king's mathematician, who was in charge of organizing the resources, noticed that some of the bags contained numbers that were not coprime. In other words, there were two adjacent numbers in the bag that shared a common factor other than 1.

The mathematician knew that this could cause problems later on, so he decided to take action. He took the bags with non-coprime numbers and replaced the two adjacent numbers with their LCM. He repeated this process for all bags with non-coprime numbers until there were no more left.

As he worked, the mathematician realized that this process could be generalized. He wanted to create an algorithm to find and replace non-coprime numbers in any array of integers. The algorithm could be used to ensure that all resources gathered for the festival were coprime, promoting unity and harmony among the tribes.

Can you help the mathematician to solve this problem?
inputFormat:
The first line contains n, size of array.
Next line contains n space separated integers.
outputFormat: Return the modified array as space separated integers.

name: Distance Problem
description:
Rajesh Bhaiya  Loves to play with arrays and their distances. This time he came up with a thought of finding the k'th smallest distance among all pairs a[i] and a[j] where  :  0 <= i < j < a.length().

The distance between a pair is defined as the absolute difference between them.
inputFormat:
First line consists of array length N and K.
Second line will have array elements.
outputFormat: The kth smallest distance.

name: Kartik Bhaiya and Signum Function
description:
Kartik Bhaiya was teaching mathematics to his students. He defined signum(x) function as follows :-

-  signum(x) is 1 if x is positive.

-  signum(x) is -1 if x is negative.

-  signum(x) is 0 if x is equal to zero.

Om also being a computer science student decided to solve a coding problem based on signum function. The problem is as follows:-

Given an array of N integers. Find the value of signum(P) where P is the product of all the elements of the array.
inputFormat: First line contains one integer N that denotes the size of the array. The second line contains N spaced integers which represent the elements of the array.
outputFormat: Print signum(P) where P is the product of all the elements of the array.

name: Trip in a Bus
description:
Monu is an engineering student. It was his summer vacation. So, he with his friends decided to go on a trip in a bus. Each bus makes multiple trips successively; that is, the next trip can start immediately after completing the current trip. Also, each bus operates independently; that is, the trips of one bus do not influence the trips of any other bus. Given an array time where arr[i] denotes the time taken by the ith bus to complete one trip.

You are also given an integer trips  which denotes the number of trips all buses should make in total. Print the minimum time required for all buses to complete at least t trips trips.

![Bus Link](https://png.pngtree.com/png-vector/20230209/ourmid/pngtree-cute-bus-clipart-png-image_6592473.png)
inputFormat:
First Line contains size of array

Second line contains space separated elements of array

Third line contains t trips
outputFormat: Integer

name: Rotated Digits
description:
You are given a number N. You have to calculate the count of good numbers between 1 to N. A good number is a number in which each digit after 180 degrees rotation is a valid digit and the number formed after rotation is different from n.
An integer  x  is a good if after rotating each digit individually by 180 degrees, we get a valid number that is different from x. Each digit must be rotated - we cannot choose to leave it alone.

A number is valid if each digit remains a digit after rotation. For example:

    0, 1, and 8 rotate to themselves,
    2 and 5 rotate to each other (in this case they are rotated in a different direction, in other words, 2 or 5 gets mirrored),
    6 and 9 rotate to each other, and
    the rest of the numbers do not rotate to any other number and become invalid.

Given an integer n, return the number of good integers in the range [1, n].

Example :

Input: n = 10

Output: 4

Explanation: There are four good numbers in the range [1, 10] : 2, 5, 6, 9.
Note that 1 and 10 are not good numbers, since they remain unchanged after rotating.
inputFormat: The number n.
outputFormat: The number of rotated digits.

name: Missing Number
description: Given an array nums containing n distinct numbers in the range [0, n], return the only number in the range that is missing from the array.
constraints:
n == nums.length
1 <= n <= 10^4

0 <= nums[i] <= n

All the numbers of nums are unique.
inputFormat:
You are given with n the number of integers.
N integers.
outputFormat: Return the missing integer

name: Bitwise AND Range Game
description: Given two integers left and right that represent the range [left, right], print the bitwise AND of all numbers in this range, inclusive.
inputFormat: First line contains two integers *left* and *right*.
outputFormat: Print Bitwise AND of the given range.

name: Allocate Bus Seats
description:
A bus has n rows of seats, numbered from 1 to n and there are ten seats in each row, labelled from 1 to 10.

Given the list of reservedSeats containing the numbers of seats already reserved, for example, reservedSeats[i] = [3,8] means the seat located in row 3 and labelled with 8 is already reserved.

Return the maximum number of four-person groups you can assign on the bus seats. A four-person group occupies four adjacent seats in one single row. Seats across an aisle (such as [3,3] and [3,4]) are not considered to be adjacent, but there is an exceptional case on which an aisle split a four-person group, in that case, the aisle split a four-person group in the middle, which means to have two people on each side.
constraints:
- 1 <= n <= 10^9

- 1 <= reservedSeats.length <= min(10*n, 10^4)

- reservedSeats[i].length == 2

- 1 <= reservedSeats[i][0] <= n

- 1 <= reservedSeats[i][1] <= 10

- All reservedSeats[i] are distinct.
inputFormat:
First line of input contains two integer n and m, number of rows and number of reserved seats.

Following m line contains two integer i and j representing that seat located in row 3 and labelled with 8 is already reserved.
outputFormat: Return single integer the maximum number of four-person groups you can assign on the bus seats.

name: XOR Result
description:
different things have different results so elemts with different bits will resultin some different result in particular range.
Given an integer n and an integer start.

Define an array nums where nums[i] = start + 2*i (0-indexed) and n == nums.length.
Return XOR.
inputFormat: You are given with the two integers.
outputFormat: you have to return the XOR.

name: Print all possible solutions to N–Queens problem
description:
The N–queens puzzle is the problem of placing N chess queens on an N × N chessboard so that no two queens threaten each other. Thus, the solution requires that no two queens share the same row, column, or diagonal.

For example, for a standard 8 × 8 chessboard, below is one such configuration:

  Q  –  –  –  –  –  –  –

  –  –  –  –  Q  –  –  –

  –  –  –  –  –  –  –  Q

  –  –  –  –  –  Q  –  –

  –  –  Q  –  –  –  –  –

  –  –  –  –  –  –  Q  –

  –  Q  –  –  –  –  –  –

  –  –  –  Q  –  –  –  –

Note that the solution exists for all natural numbers n, except for n = 2 and n = 3.
inputFormat: An integer N.
outputFormat: N x N matrix after placing N queens

name: Count distinct elements in every window
description: Given an array A of size N and an integer K, return the of the count of distinct numbers in all windows of size k.
inputFormat: The first line of input contains an integer T denoting the number of test cases. Then T test cases follow. Each test case contains two integers N and K. Then in the next line are N space-separated values of the array A.
outputFormat: For each test case in a new line print, space-separated values denoting counts of distinct numbers in all windows of size k in the array A[].

name: Maximum of Minimum for Every Window
description: Given an integer array of size n, find the maximum of the minimum’s of every window size in the array. Note that window size varies from 1 to n.
inputFormat: The First Line contains an Integer as Size of the Array.
outputFormat: Print the Maximum of Minimum for every window separated by space.

name: All Possible Palindrome Partitions
description: You are given a string *s*, partition the string *s* such that every substring of the partition is a palindrome. Print all possible palindrome partitioning of *s*.
constraints:
1<= s.length <= 16

*s* contains only lowercase English Alphabets
inputFormat: First line of input contains a string s.
outputFormat: Print all possible palindrome partitioning of the input string.

name: Palindrome Break
description:
You are given a palindrome, which is a string of lowercase English letters. Your task is to find the lexicographically smallest non-palindromic string that can be obtained by replacing exactly one character in the given palindrome.

If such a string cannot be formed, return an empty string. Otherwise, return the resulting string after replacing one character in the palindrome.

A string is considered lexicographically smaller than another string if it comes first in a dictionary. In other words, for two strings of the same length, the lexicographically smaller string is the one where the character at the first differing position is smaller.

For example, "abcc" is lexicographically smaller than "abcd" because the first position they differ is at the fourth character, and 'c' is smaller than 'd'.
constraints: The length of the string is less than 1000.
inputFormat: The palindromic string.
outputFormat: The string in output format.

name: Good Strings
description: You're given three strings: s1, s2, and evil, all of length n. Your task is to find the count of strings of length n that are lexicographically between s1 and s2 (inclusive), and do not contain the substring evil. Since the answer might be large, return the count modulo 109 + 7.
constraints:
s1.length == n

s2.length == n

s1 <= s2

1 <= n <= 500

1 <= evil.length <= 50

All strings consist of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat:
First Line contains size of strings s1 and s2

Second line contains string s1

Third line contains string s2

Fourth line contains string evil
outputFormat: Integer

name: OR Operation
description:
You are given an array of integers, where each element represents a number. Additionally, you are given an integer x, representing the maximum number of times you can perform an operation on the array. In each operation, you can choose any element of the array and multiply it by 2.

Your task is to find the maximum possible value of the bitwise OR operation between all elements of the array after performing at most x operations.

In other words, you need to determine the maximum value that can be obtained by bitwise OR-ing all elements of the array after potentially doubling some elements up to x times.
inputFormat:
First Line contains Size of Array

Second Line contains space separated elements of array

Third Line contains integer x
outputFormat: Print Integer

name: String Match
description: You're given two strings, "a" and "b". Your task is to find out how many times you need to repeat string "a" so that string "b" becomes a part of the repeated string "a". If it's impossible for "b" to be a part of "a" after repeating it, return -1. For example, if "a" is "abc" and "b" is "cab", you need to determine how many times you need to repeat "abc" to contain "cab".
constraints:
1 4

a and b consist of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat:
First Line contains String a

Second Line contains String b
outputFormat: Integer

name: Puzzle on Cards
description:
Monu Bhaiya went to club on New Year. There he was enjoying with his friends. Suddenly they came across a game on cards. It was a puzzle game. The game was as follows

Given a sorted deck of cards numbered 1 to N.

1) Pick up 1 card and put it on the back of the deck.

2) Now, pick up another card, it turns out to be card number 1, we put it outside the deck.

3) Now pick up 2 cards and put it on the back of the deck.

4) Now pick up another card and it turns out to be card numbered 2, we put it outside the deck. ...

Perform this step until the last card.

If such an arrangement of decks is possible, output the arrangement, if it is not possible for a particular value of N then output -1.

Now the condition is if Monu Bhaiya was able to give correct answer to every case then he would win a movie ticket. Help monu bhaiya to design the code to solve the above puzzle on cards so that he could win the movie ticket.
inputFormat: Input a number n
outputFormat: Print List

name: Monu bhaiya going to classroom
description:
While going for classes Monu bhaiya loves to use stair case in place of lift.There are N steps in which a number P[i] (for i-th step) is written on it. For each step he can either proceed to next step(i+1) or he can jump P[i] steps from that step(to i+P[i]-th step). If the number written on the step is less than 0 , the he can come down that many number of steps or climb one step up.

Now, he is going to climb from 0th step.Print the minimum number of jumps he will take to reach in the classroom(at the top).If it is not possible to reach in the classroom(at the top) then print -1.

Note : Jump >  N is an invalid move.
inputFormat:
First line is a number T representing  number of test cases.

For T test cases the first line is an integer 'N'.

 For T test cases the next line consist an array P containing of N space separated integers.
outputFormat: Print an integer for each test cases.

name: Circular Game
description:
In a land filled with electrical charges, there were N charging stations arranged in a circular route. Each charging station had a certain amount of charge, represented by the array charge[i].

You have a car with an unlimited battery capacity and it costs cost[i] of charge to travel from the ith station to its next (i + 1)th station. You started your journey with an empty battery at one of the charging stations.

Your goal was to find a starting charging station's index from where you could travel around the circuit once in the rightward direction without running out of charge. If such a starting station existed, you wanted to return its index; otherwise, you would return -1. It was guaranteed that if a solution existed, it would be unique.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the integer value N representing the charging Station.

The second line contains n space-separated integers with the amount of charge in each charging Station.

The third line contains the integer value N representing the cost array.

The fourth line contains n space-separated integer representing the cost to travel from the ith station to the next (i+1) station.
outputFormat: Find a starting charging station's index from where you could travel around the circuit once in the rightward direction without running out of charge. If such a starting station existed, you wanted to return its index; otherwise, you would return -1.

name: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock - IV
description:
You are given an integer array **prices** where prices[i] is the price of a given stock on the ith day, and an integer **k**.

Find the **maximum profit** you can achieve. You may complete **at most** k transactions.

***Note: You may not engage in multiple transactions simultaneously (i.e., you must sell the stock before you buy again).***
inputFormat:
First line contains two space separated integers n (size of the array) and k

Second line contains an integer array prices.
outputFormat: print the maximum profit you can achieve.

name: Mr. Block’s Valentine’s Day Mystery 💖
description:
It was Valentine’s Day at Coding Blocks, and the air was filled with love and excitement. 💕 Mr. Block, the legendary coder, sat in his favorite chair, sipping hot chocolate ☕ and staring at two mysterious love letters 💌—one from Sophie (s) 💃 and the other from Tara (t) 💁‍♀️.

Sophie’s letter was short and sweet 🍭, just a few words strung together with warmth. Tara’s, on the other hand, was longer 📜, filled with poetry and secret messages 🕵️‍♂️. Mr. Block had a curious thought:

"Could Sophie’s letter be secretly hidden within Tara’s words? 🤔 Was Sophie’s message a subsequence of Tara’s letter?"

A subsequence, as Mr. Block explained to his students 🎓, is when the letters of Sophie’s message appear in the same order 📌 inside Tara’s, though they might be scattered around ✨. If he could find Sophie’s message inside Tara’s, it meant the two were meant to be—a perfect coding pair! 💑

So, with the power of algorithms ⚡ and a heart full of curiosity ❤️, Mr. Block set out to solve the Valentine’s Day mystery 🕵️‍♀️:

"Is Sophie’s letter a subsequence of Tara’s? If yes, love is in the air!  If not, well… maybe it’s time for Sophie to write a new message. 😔"

Will Mr. Block find love hidden in the code? 💻 Let’s find out! 🚀✨
constraints:
0 <= s.length <= 100

0 <= t.length <= 10^4

s and t consist only of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: Input strings s and t
outputFormat: true or false

name: Snake Loves Diagonal Move
description:
In the land of Coding Blocks, Mr. Block encountered a peculiar m x n Matrix. A snake, fond of diagonal moves, began its journey at the top-left corner (0, 0) and traversed the matrix in an alternate diagonal pattern. With each move, the snake visited the next element along the diagonal until it reached the bottom-right corner (m-1, n-1).

![Matrix](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/04/10/diag1-grid.jpg)
inputFormat:
First Line contains two space separated integers N (Rows) and M (cols) .

Next N lines consists of  space separated each row elements of matrix
outputFormat: Print all element of matrix in alternate diagonal order.

name: School Trip
description:
Emily is a middle school student . Her school decided to go on a trip. They visit a really big sanctury. As they have very limited time. Emily teacher comes with a idea to split up the students in groups to visit maximum places.

Trip consist of total N students . Each of them have number A[i] print on their T-shirt. Two students can have T-shirt with same number . Emily's teacher decided to split all N students in k groups numbered from 1 to k. Each student must be in exactly in one group. Grouping must be consecutive i.e group the students in the order they came.

Let h(i) represent the group number ith student belong to. Happiness of the trip is equals to summation of A[i]⋅h(i) for 1<=i<=N.

Calculate the maximum happiness can be achive by spliting N students in k groups.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers n and k (1≤k≤n≤3*1e^5).
The second line contains n integers A1,A2,…,An (|Ai|≤1e^6) where Ai represent the number written on T-shirt of ith student.
outputFormat: Print the maximum Happiness can achieve by dividing the students into k groups.

name: Monster Rage
description:
Sunny loves playing games.He decided to play recently launched game called **Monster Rage**.This game consist of N Monsters numbered from 1 to N.Game is completed when all the monsters are eliminated.To eliminate a monster you have to hit him with a specificed type bullet.

Sunny plays this game every so often , so he knew that to kill the ith (1<=i<=N) monster he have to shoot it with Ai type bullet.In game sunny character has a gun with size of magzine equals to K (at a time only k bullets can be loaded in the gun) which is empty initially .If magzine doesn't contain the Ai type bullet for ith Monster Sunny can purchase it from in-game shop by spending 1 BP.After eliminating every monster Sunny has two option either remove bullet from the magzine or leave it as it is.

One bullet type can be used to kill multiple specified monster if it is inside magzine.

Sunny has to complete its homework , so he asked your help to complete the game.What is the minimum cost(in BP) required to complete the game?
inputFormat: The first line of input will contain two integers n and k (1 ≤ n, k ≤ 400000). The second line will contain n integers a1, a2, ..., an (1 ≤ ai ≤ n) – type of bullet required to kill ith monster.
outputFormat: On a single line print the minimum cost of buying bullets from in-game store so as to complete the game.

name: Mr. Blocks' Binary Sorting Adventure
description:
In the land of Byteland, Mr. Blocks needs to organize a line of citizens. Each citizen wears a uniform with a number written on it . Mr. Blocks wants the line sorted by the number of 1's in the binary representation of the number written on their uniform,If citizens have the same number of 1's in binary representation, they should simply line up in order by the number written on their uniform. Can you help Mr. Blocks sort his line?

Note - Please Ignore Test Case Input1 / Output1 as text while taking input and while showing output.
inputFormat:
the first line contains one integer n — the number of citizen;
the second line contains n integers a1,a2,…,an where ai is the number written on the uniform of i-th citizen.
outputFormat: Output an array sorted according to given condition.

name: Colorful Conundrum: Mrs. Blocks vs. Mr. Blocks
description:
In a colorful line-up of n pieces, each colored 'A' or 'B', Mrs. Blocks and Mr. Blocks engage in a strategic game. With alternating turns, Mrs. Blocks starts, aiming to remove 'A'-colored pieces only if their neighbors match ( if both its neighbors are also colored 'A' ) . Conversely, Mr. Blocks targets only 'B'-colored pieces only if their neighbors match ( if both its neighbors are also colored 'B' )  .
 The game continues until one player cannot make a move, declaring the opponent the winner.

Note :  Mrs. Blocks and Mr. Blocks cannot remove pieces from the edge of the line.

name: Bhupendra Jogi - The Postman
description:
After coming back from USA, Bhupendra Jogi decides to join  Government Job. For this he decides to prepare for India Post for the position of Postman. He with his hard work finally cracks the exam and joins Post Office as a Postman.

Now One Day he was assigned a task to arrange envelopes one into another. Now, One envelope fits into another one  if and only if both the width and height of one envelope is greater than the other envelope's width and height.

Given a 2D array of integers arr where arr[i] = [wi, hi] represents the width and the height of an envelope.

Now, Your task is to help Bhupendra Jogi and print maximum number of envelopes he can put one inside the other.

Second Line contains Number of Columns

Third Line contains elements of Matrix
outputFormat: Integer

name: Unraveling the Mysterious Message
description:
You're an intrepid codebreaker on a mission to crack a mysterious message sent by a rival spy agency. The message is written in a strange code where each number stands for a letter in the alphabet.

But here's the twist: the code isn't as straightforward as  A = 1, B = 2,C=3 .......Z=26  and so on. Nope, it's more like a puzzle! You see, the numbers can be grouped in different ways, and each grouping might give you a different message.

So, your job is to figure out all the different ways you can group the numbers and decode them back into letters. With each decoding, you're getting closer to uncovering the secrets hidden within the message. But time is ticking, and the enemy won't wait forever. Can you crack the code before it's too late? The fate of the mission rests in your hands!

 For example, "11106" can be mapped into:

"AAJF" with the grouping (1 1 10 6)
"KJF" with the grouping (11 10 6)

Note: that the grouping (1 11 06) is invalid because "06" cannot be mapped into 'F' since "6" is different from "06".
 Please Ignore Test Case Input 1 as a text while taking i.e while taking

Given a string s containing only digits, return the number of ways to decode it.
The test cases are generated so that the answer fits in a 32-bit integer.

outputFormat: Output the number of ways to decode the string.

name: The Quest of Mr. Blocks: Journey to Transform Words
description:
In the quaint village of Lexonia, Mr. Blocks, a curious character with a penchant for puzzles, stumbled upon an intriguing challenge. The village was buzzing with excitement about transforming words, and Mr. Blocks couldn't resist diving into the mystery.

The task was to transform one word into another, but there was a catch – each transformation could only change one letter at a time, and every intermediate word must be a valid word from the village dictionary.

With his trusty dictionary in hand, Mr. Blocks set out on his adventure. His journey began with the word "beginWord" and ended with "endWord." Along the way, he could swap letters to form new words, but he had to ensure that each word he encountered was in the village dictionary.

As Mr. Blocks delved deeper into the challenge, he realized that finding the shortest transformation sequence required careful planning and strategy. He navigated through the wordList, meticulously altering letters one by one, until he reached his destination.

Now, join Mr. Blocks on his quest as he explores the world of word transformations and discovers the shortest path from "beginWord" to "endWord." Will he succeed in unraveling the puzzle, or will he encounter unforeseen obstacles along the way? Only time will tell in this thrilling journey of wit and wordplay.

Given two words, beginWord and endWord, and a dictionary wordList, return the number of words in the shortest transformation sequence from beginWord to endWord, or 0 if no such sequence exists.

Note : Please Ignore Test Case Input / Output as text while taking input and while showing output.

1 <= n <= 10

endWord.length == beginWord.length==n

1 <= wordList.length <= 5000

wordList[i].length == beginWord.length

beginWord, endWord, and wordList[i] consist of lowercase English letters.

beginWord != endWord

All the words in wordList are unique.

In first line take a integer n.
Take input of string beginWord.
Take input of string endWord
Take a integer k as input (k=wordList size) .
At last take a array of strings as a input s1,s2....,sk ( elements of wordList)
outputFormat: Output the number of words in the shortest transformation sequence from beginWord to endWord, or 0 if no such sequence exists.

name: Navigating Hazardous Terrain:
description:
You are given an n * m 0-indexed grid representing a landscape. You are currently located at cell "S" and your goal is to reach cell "D". The landscape consists of the following types of cells:

".": Empty cells.

"X": Stone cells.

"*": Flooded cells.

You can move to a neighboring cell (up, down, left, or right) each second. However, empty cells neighboring flooded cells will become flooded themselves in the next second.

You cannot move onto flooded cells or cells that will become flooded in the same second you step onto them.
Your task is to find the minimum time it takes to reach the destination in seconds, or return -1 if it is impossible to reach the destination.

Take the input of the n*m matrix as string

name: Mayank's Mystical Harmonization Quest
description:
In a mystical land, there are two arrays named "Magics" and "Elixirs,"  both of the arrays have equal length n  each containing n positive integers.

Mayank, have been granted the ability to perform a fascinating operation any number of times:

Mayank can increase or decrease any element of the array Magics by 1, each with its own mystical cost.
The cost of performing one operation on the ith element is stored in the array Elixirs at index i.

Your task is to uncover the minimum total cost required to harmonize (equalize all elements)  all the elements of the array Magics, aligning them to the symphony of magic that flows through the land.

Note :  use long long for answer

In second line take input of Magics array a1,a2.....an
In third line take input of Elixirs array b1,b2,b3....bn  .

name: Arrayville and Mr. Block
description:
In a quaint village named **Arrayville**, there lived an array of integers called **"arr,"** filled with unique personalities. One day, a mysterious integer named "k" arrived, causing a stir. The villagers needed to remove **exactly k elements** to restore peace.
In other words we have   an array of integers arr and an integer k. Find the least number of unique integers after removing exactly k elements.
inputFormat:
First line contain n and  k .

Second line contain n space separated integer of array.
outputFormat: Output the least number of unique integers after removing exactly k elements.

name: Abhishek Bhaiya and String
description:
In the bustling binary town, Rajesh Bhaiya was known for his knack for flipping things around. One day, he received a peculiar request from Abhishek Bhaiya , the town's wise mathematician. Abhishek Bhaiya  had a binary string called "target," and he needed Rajesh's Bhaiya help to transform another string "s," of length n (that is initially set to all zeros)  into target string.
* In one operation, you can pick an index i where 0 <= i < n and flip all bits in the inclusive range [i, n - 1]. Flip means changing '0' to '1' and '1' to '0'.

Return the minimum number of operations needed to make s equal to target.
constraints:
* n == target.length
* 1 5
* target[i] is either '0' or '1'.
inputFormat:

description:

The steps of the insertion sort algorithm:

Insertion sort iterates, consuming one input element each repetition and growing a sorted output list.
At each iteration, insertion sort removes one element from the input data, finds the location it belongs within the sorted list and inserts it there.
It repeats until no input elements remain.

accountHolder: The name of the person who owns the

withdraw(int amount): Deducts the specified amount from the account balance, if sufficient funds are available. Returns true if successful, false if insufficient funds.

getAccountNumber(): Returns the account number.

accounts: An array of Account objects, storing all the accounts in the bank.

Creating Accounts: Users can create accounts with a unique account number, holder's name, and an initial balance.

description: Given the root of a binary tree, the value of a target node target, and an integer k, return an array of the values of all nodes that have a distance k from the target node.
constraints:
The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 500].

0 <= Node.val <= 500

All the values Node.val are unique.

*target* is the value of one of the nodes in the tree.

0 <= k <= 1000
inputFormat:
The tree is built from a string representation of the tree which is given as input.

Each node is separated by a space. 'N' represents a null node.

Second line contains *target* and the *K*.
outputFormat: Print all nodes that are at a distance K.

name: Recipe Management System
description:
You are tasked with building a Recipe Management System using Object-Oriented Programming. The system should manage recipes, ingredients, categories, and chefs. Chefs can create new recipes, categorize them, and add necessary ingredients. The system should allow users to search for recipes based on categories or ingredients.

Person Class and Basic Details

Create a Person class that handles basic details for chefs. Implement getter and setter methods for the attributes.

Chef Class for Recipe Creation

Ingredient and Category Classes

Recipe Class with Ingredients and Instructions

RecipeManager Class for System Management

Implement the RecipeManager class that manages the recipes, chefs, categories, and ingredients.

name: Online Movie Rental System
description:
You are tasked with designing a simplified Online Movie Rental System to manage movie rentals. The system should keep track of movies available for rent and customer rental history. The system should allow customers to rent and return movies. It should also allow the system administrators (via a MovieStore class) to manage the list of available movies by adding or removing movies from the store and searching for movies by their unique ID.

Requirements:

Movie Class:

Attributes:

movieID: Unique identifier for each movie.

title: The title of the movie.

rentalPrice: The price to rent the movie.

available: A boolean indicating if the movie is available for rent (True if available, False if rented).

Methods:

rentMovie(): Marks the movie as rented (sets available to False).

returnMovie(): Marks the movie as returned (sets available to True).

displayMovieInfo(): Displays detailed information about the movie.

MovieStore Class:

Attributes:

movies: A collection of movies available in the store (stored as individual references, not in a list).

customers: A collection of customers (stored individually, not in a list).

Methods:

addMovie(Movie movie): Adds a movie to the store.

removeMovie(int movieID): Removes a movie from the store by its unique movie ID.

searchMovie(int movieID): Searches and returns a movie by its unique ID.

viewInventory(): Displays all the movies in the store with their availability status.

Customer Class:

Attributes:

customerID: Unique identifier for each customer.

name: The name of the customer.

rentalHistory: Collection of movies the customer has rented (stored individually, not in a list).

Methods:

rentMovie(Movie movie): Rents a movie if available.

returnMovie(Movie movie): Returns a previously rented movie.

viewRentalHistory(): Displays all movies rented by the customer.

Your task is to implement this system and take input of movies and rental queries and print the expected output and print the users rental history in the end
inputFormat:

Movie Store Setup:
Number of Movies (m): An integer representing the total number of movies to be added to the store.

name: Merge two sorted array
description: Given two sorted arrays, merge them into a single sorted array in-place . The merged array should maintain the sorted order.
inputFormat:
The input consists of two sorted arrays:

- The first line contains an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 104), which represents the number of elements in the first array.
- The second line contains n space-separated integers, representing the sorted elements of the first array, in non-decreasing order.

name: Sum of Squares
description:
Task

You are given an integer n, and your task is to find the least number of perfect squares that sum to n for each test case.
A perfect square is a number of the form x², where x is a non-negative integer.
inputFormat:
- The first line contains an integer t, representing the number of test cases.

- Each of the next t lines contains an integer n, representing the value for which you need to find the least number of perfect squares.
outputFormat: For each test case, return the least number of perfect squares that sum to n.

name: Prime Number
description: Write a program to check if a number N is prime or not.
inputFormat: The first line contains a integer N.
outputFormat: Print "Prime" if the number is prime otherwise print "Not Prime".

name: Detect a Cycle in Directed Graph
description:
You are given a directed graph with n vertices and m edges. Your task is to determine whether the graph contains a cycle.

A cycle in a directed graph is a path that starts and ends at the same vertex, with each edge and vertex in the cycle traversed only once.
inputFormat:
- The first line contains two integers n (number of vertices) and m (number of edges).
- The next m lines each contain two integers u and v, denoting a directed edge from vertex u to vertex v.Vertices are numbered from 0 to n-1.
The graph may contain self-loops and multiple edges between two vertices.
outputFormat: Output "YES" if the graph contains a cycle, and "NO" otherwise.

name: Buzz Day Sale
description:
Karan, who owns a shop at an exhibition, is planning to launch a promotion where customers receive free items with the purchase of specific items. He has chosen a few items for this special offer, which he's called the "Buzz Day Sale." Additionally, there are unlimited quantities available for each item type.

He assigned a unique ID to each item based on its worth and put up a board that reads, "For every purchase of an item with ID K, all other items with IDs that are factors of K will be free."

Veda visited Karan's shop on Buzz Day with the aim of acquiring as many items as possible while carrying a limited amount of money, A. If there are several ways to maximize the number of free items, she will strive to maximize the total worth of the items she receives freely.

Given the IDs of all the items offered in the sale and their costs, determine the maximum number of items Veda can receive for free and the maximum total worth of those items.
constraints:
- 1 ≤ N ≤ 500
- 1 ≤ ID of each item ≤ 1000
- 1 ≤ cost of each item ≤ 1000
- 1 ≤ Amount Veda holds ≤ 1000
- Each ID is unique.
inputFormat:
- The first line contains a single integer, N, denoting the number of items in the sale.
- The second line contains N space-separated integers, representing the ID of each item.
- The third line contains N space-separated integers, representing the cost of each item.
- The last line contains a single integer, A, denoting the amount Veda has.
outputFormat:
Print two space-separated integers representing the maximum number of free items Veda can obtain and the maximum total worth of those items given the amount she has.

Maximize the number of free items first then maximize the total worth of free items.

name: Alice went to Island
description:
Alice went to an island and saw that an island is surrounded by water and is formed by connecting adjacent lands horizontally or vertically. Assume all four edges of the grid are all surrounded by water.

Given an m x n 2D binary grid grid which represents a map of '1's (land) and '0's (water), Print the number of islands.
constraints:
m == grid.length

n == grid[i].length

1 <= m, n <= 300

grid[i][j] is '0' or '1'.
inputFormat:
Two integers m and n representing number of rows and columns in the matrix.

m*n elements representing matrix
outputFormat: An integer representing number of islands

name: Form Alternating String
description:
You are given a binary string made up of 0s and 1s, along with an array of integers representing the worth of each character in the string.

Your task is to make the longest alternating string possible with the removal of characters such that the sum of the worth of the characters removed  is minimum possible.

Specifically, you need to:
- Form the longest alternating string possible by removing zero or more characters.
- Maximize the worth of this longest alternating string.
- Determine the sum of the worth of the characters that need to be removed to achieve this.A string is considered an alternating string if it alternates between 0 and 1 (e.g., 010101 or 101010).
constraints:
- 1 ≤ N ≤ 200,000
- The binary string consists of 0s and 1s only.
- 1 ≤ worth of each character ≤ 109
inputFormat:
- First line contains an integer N, the length of the binary string .
- Second line contains a binary string S of length N.
- The third line contains N  integers representing the worth of each character in the binary string .
outputFormat: Print a single integer representing the sum of the worth of the characters that must be deleted to transform the given binary string into the largest alternating string with the maximum worth.

name: Dance Revolution - Minimizing Foot Movements
description:
Dance Revolution is the pioneering series of the rhythm and dance genre in video games.

The core gameplay involves placing your feet on certain tiles according to the instructions displayed on the screen.

In this problem, there are four tiles, up, down, right, and left. You can move one leg at a time. Initially, you can place your feet on any tiles. Instructions will contain the list of tiles, where you must place one of your feet, one instruction after another.

Given the instruction to place your feet, find the minimum number of times you must move your legs to different tiles following the instruction. You can start with placing your legs at any position
inputFormat:
The input consists of:

- The first line contains a single integer N, the total number of instructions.
- The next N lines contain the instructions, one instruction per line. Each instruction is one of up, down, right, or left.
outputFormat: Output a single integer representing the minimum number of movements required to follow all instructions.
